Python standard library provider proposals

Python 3.15.2 documentation. 297 of 297 current modules in scope have a source-grounded proposal.

The bindings and rankings are estate design proposals. Removed modules are identified separately.

Python library reference | Module index

__future__

Python Runtime Services

Python documentation

introspect_future_feature: given a feature name, return its optional release, mandatory release (or null), and compiler flag by reading the _Feature instance from the __future__ module, without compiling or importing user code.

APIs

  • __future__._Feature.getOptionalRelease
  • __future__._Feature.getMandatoryRelease
  • __future__._Feature.compiler_flag
  • getattr(__future__, name)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"feature_name":{"type":"string","description":"Name of a __future__ feature attribute, e.g. \u0027annotations\u0027 or \u0027generator_stop\u0027."}},"required":["feature_name"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"feature_name":{"type":"string"},"optional_release":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["integer","string"]},"minItems":5,"maxItems":5},"mandatory_release":{"type":["array","null"],"items":{"type":["integer","string"]},"minItems":5,"maxItems":5},"compiler_flag":{"type":"integer"},"is_mandatory":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["feature_name","optional_release","mandatory_release","compiler_flag","is_mandatory"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only introspection of the in-process __future__ module; no compilation, no code execution, no filesystem or network access, no mutation of interpreter state.

Constraints Requires a CPython-compatible runtime exposing __future__._Feature with getOptionalRelease/getMandatoryRelease/compiler_flag; release tuples follow sys.version_info 5-tuple form; mandatory_release may be null (e.g. annotations); behavior is interpreter-version dependent and must not be assumed stable across versions.

Failure modes

  • UnknownFeature: feature_name is not an attribute of __future__ or is not a _Feature instance (e.g. '_Feature' class itself, dunder names).
  • InvalidInput: feature_name is not a string or is empty.
  • AttributeError surfaced if the runtime's __future__ lacks expected attributes (unexpected interpreter).

Ranked use cases

  1. Build a capability that reports which future features are still optional vs mandatory for the running interpreter version.
  2. Generate correct compile() flags for dynamically compiled code by mapping feature names to compiler_flag values.
  3. Audit source files' future imports against the documented optional/mandatory release table for compatibility checks.
  4. Produce executable documentation of __future__ contents for tooling that analyzes import statements.
  5. Detect features with null mandatory release (e.g. annotations) to warn about planned deprecation/removal.

__main__

Python Runtime Services

Python documentation

inspect_main_namespace: given a list of attribute names, report which are defined in the current top-level __main__ namespace (via import __main__ and dir(__main__)), without executing or mutating top-level code.

APIs

  • import __main__ (imports the top-level environment's namespace module, per the 'import __main__' section)
  • dir(__main__) (enumerates names present in the __main__ namespace, as used in the did_user_define_their_name example)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"names":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":1}},"required":["names"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"defined":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"undefined":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"mainModuleName":{"type":"string"}},"required":["defined","undefined","mainModuleName"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only introspection of the in-process __main__ namespace; no top-level code is executed, no names are added or removed, no files or environment are modified.

Constraints Only meaningful inside a running Python interpreter where a __main__ module exists in sys.modules; results reflect the current process's top-level environment and differ between script, -m, -c, stdin and REPL invocations; not applicable to .zip root __main__.py edge cases described in the excerpt; no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • Empty or missing 'names' array rejected by schema validation
  • Non-string entries in 'names' rejected by schema validation
  • ImportError if __main__ cannot be imported in the current interpreter context
  • AttributeError/TypeError if dir() on the __main__ module fails unexpectedly
  • Names present but bound to None or unset sentinels are reported as defined (presence, not value, is checked)

Ranked use cases

  1. Guard script-only code paths by checking whether expected top-level names exist before running entry logic
  2. Diagnose why a module behaves differently when run as __main__ versus imported
  3. Support test harnesses that verify a program's top-level namespace is populated as expected
  4. Enable REPL/notebook tooling to detect user-defined variables in the __main__ scope
  5. Assist debugging tools (like pdb-style consumers of __main__) in enumerating available top-level names

Source digest sha256:bfbca6928acd770de15a707708c9dc1e078af414a8c30fbd57ec440de8e9f6d5

_thread

Concurrent Execution

Python documentation

Acquire a low-level _thread lock with bounded blocking and timeout, returning acquisition status and lock state, without starting threads or emitting signals.

APIs

  • _thread.allocate_lock
  • _thread.LockType.acquire
  • _thread.LockType.release
  • _thread.LockType.locked
  • _thread.TIMEOUT_MAX

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"blocking":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"timeout":{"type":"number","default":-1},"releaseAfter":{"type":"boolean","default":false}},"required":["blocking"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"acquired":{"type":"boolean"},"lockedAfter":{"type":"boolean"},"released":{"type":"boolean"},"timeoutUsed":{"type":"number"}},"required":["acquired","lockedAfter","released"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Creates and manipulates an in-process lock object only; may block the calling thread up to the timeout; optionally releases the lock before returning. No threads are started, no signals are emitted, no files or network resources are touched.

Constraints In-process only; lock state is not shared across processes. Timeout semantics and signal interruption of acquires differ by platform (POSIX vs Windows, changed in 3.14). _thread.TIMEOUT_MAX bounds the timeout. Lock ownership is not tracked, so release may occur from a different thread. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError when timeout is specified while blocking is false
  • OverflowError when timeout exceeds _thread.TIMEOUT_MAX
  • RuntimeError from _thread.error on thread-specific lock errors
  • RuntimeError when releasing a lock not currently held
  • TypeError when timeout is not a number or blocking is not a boolean

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders wrapping a bounded mutex acquire/release primitive for shared-state coordination in generated code
  2. Test harnesses that verify lock contention behavior with non-blocking and timed acquires
  3. Safe serialization of short critical sections around shared caches in worker-style scripts
  4. Diagnostics that probe lock state (locked) to detect deadlocks or leaked locks
  5. Portable timeout-bounded synchronization shims that respect _thread.TIMEOUT_MAX across platforms

Source digest sha256:8cb2e4d66fb79be32cfc768abd73180a88e8a3cdb20fdd682ae43beccbf95d7b

_tkinter

Graphical user interfaces with Tk

Python documentation

introspect_widget_options: given a live Tk widget reference, return its configuration option names and, optionally, the full 5-tuple metadata for each option, using the documented configure()/keys() introspection API.

APIs

  • tkinter.Misc.configure
  • tkinter.Misc.keys
  • tkinter.Misc.cget
  • tkinter.TclError

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"widget":{"type":"object","description":"Live tkinter widget or Tk root object reference"},"include_details":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"option_filter":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional subset of option names to return"}},"required":["widget"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"option_names":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"options":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":5,"maxItems":5}},"widget_class":{"type":"string"}},"required":["option_names","widget_class"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only introspection of the Tcl interpreter; no widget state, geometry, or display is modified. No files, network, or subprocesses are touched.

Constraints Requires a live Tk instance and a running or reachable Tcl interpreter; _tkinter is an optional binary module and may be absent from a given CPython build. Tcl/Tk >= 8.5.12 required. GUI/display availability depends on platform (X11, Cocoa, GDI); headless environments without a display will fail at Tk() creation. Calls from non-creating threads require the event loop to be processing events. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • TclError raised when the widget has been destroyed or its Tcl interpreter is gone
  • TclError raised when an unknown option name is passed to cget()
  • ValueError/KeyError when option_filter contains names not present on the widget
  • RuntimeError or hang if called from a non-creating thread while the Tcl event loop is not running
  • Returned values are strings; type coercion (getboolean/getint/getdouble) may raise ValueError

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders can enumerate a widget's configurable options to auto-generate typed configuration schemas for GUI automation agents
  2. Diff option sets between widget classes (e.g. ttk.Button vs ttk.Frame) to discover widget-specific capabilities
  3. Validate user-supplied option dictionaries before applying them, avoiding TclError at runtime
  4. Introspect default vs current values to snapshot and restore widget state for reproducible UI tests
  5. Drive documentation/tooling that maps Tkinter options to underlying Tcl/Tk man-page entries

abc

Python Runtime Services

Python documentation

Inspect an abstract base class: given a class object reference, report whether it is an ABCMeta-based class, its abstract method names, whether it is instantiable, and the current ABC cache token.

APIs

  • abc.ABCMeta
  • abc.get_cache_token
  • abc.update_abstractmethods
  • abc.abstractmethod

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"class_ref":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path of the class to inspect, e.g. \u0027collections.abc.Mapping\u0027"},"include_cache_token":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to include the current ABC cache token"}},"required":["class_ref"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"class_ref":{"type":"string"},"is_abcmeta_class":{"type":"boolean"},"abstract_methods":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"is_instantiable":{"type":"boolean"},"cache_token":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["class_ref","is_abcmeta_class","abstract_methods","is_instantiable"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only introspection; imports the target module into the current interpreter, which may execute module-level code. No mutation of the class or ABC registry.

Constraints Requires a live Python interpreter with the abc module (CPython 3.4+ for get_cache_token, 3.10+ for update_abstractmethods). Cache token is process-local and opaque; not comparable across processes. Importing arbitrary modules may be disallowed on restricted workers.

Failure modes

  • ImportError or AttributeError if class_ref cannot be resolved
  • TypeError if resolved object is not a class
  • PermissionError if module import is restricted by sandbox policy
  • ValueError if class_ref is malformed

Ranked use cases

  1. Validate that a plugin class fully implements a required ABC before registration in a SideFX pipeline tool
  2. Enumerate unimplemented abstract methods to generate actionable error messages for asset authors
  3. Detect ABC cache invalidation via token changes to decide when to re-validate registered virtual subclasses
  4. Audit third-party or built-in classes for interface conformance without instantiating them
  5. Drive dynamic class-decorator workflows that call update_abstractmethods after patching methods

annotationlib

Python Runtime Services

Python documentation

get_annotations_safe: retrieve an object's annotations in a caller-selected format (VALUE, FORWARDREF, or STRING) via annotationlib.get_annotations, returning a normalized mapping of annotation names to stringified representations plus per-key resolution status, without ever evaluating untrusted input beyond what the requested format requires.

APIs

  • annotationlib.get_annotations(obj, *, globals=None, locals=None, eval_str=False, format=Format.VALUE) — main entry point that computes the annotations dict for a module, class, or callable in the requested format
  • annotationlib.Format (IntEnum: VALUE=1, VALUE_WITH_FAKE_GLOBALS=2, FORWARDREF=3, STRING=4) — selects the annotation retrieval format
  • annotationlib.ForwardRef — proxy for unresolved forward references; exposes __forward_arg__ and evaluate()
  • annotationlib.annotations_to_string(annotations) — converts a runtime annotations dict to a string-only dict
  • annotationlib.type_repr(value) — converts arbitrary values to STRING-format-suitable representations

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"target":{"type":"object","description":"Reference to the object whose annotations are requested; must be resolvable by the host, e.g. a module name, a dotted class path, or a callable identifier.","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["module","class","function"]},"qualname":{"type":"string","minLength":1}},"required":["kind","qualname"],"additionalProperties":false},"format":{"type":"string","enum":["VALUE","FORWARDREF","STRING"],"default":"FORWARDREF"},"eval_str":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"include_forwardref_args":{"type":"boolean","default":true}},"required":["target"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"target":{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string"},"qualname":{"type":"string"}},"required":["kind","qualname"]},"format":{"type":"string","enum":["VALUE","FORWARDREF","STRING"]},"annotations":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"object","properties":{"rendered":{"type":"string"},"resolved":{"type":"boolean"},"forward_arg":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["rendered","resolved"]}},"count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["target","format","annotations","count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only introspection of the target object's annotations. May execute arbitrary code contained in annotations (annotate functions, eval of forward references) depending on the requested format; no persistent state is modified by the operation itself, but annotation code may have arbitrary side effects.

Constraints Requires Python 3.14+ where annotationlib exists; behavior depends on the target's annotation semantics (stock, stringified via __future__ annotations, or deferred). STRING and FORWARDREF formats are not safe on untrusted code. VALUE_WITH_FAKE_GLOBALS is internal and must not be requested. eval_str is only valid with VALUE. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • TypeError when target is not a callable, class, module, or object with __annotate__/__annotations__
  • NameError (or other evaluation error) when format=VALUE and an annotation references an undefined name
  • ZeroDivisionError or other runtime errors from unsupported expressions evaluated under VALUE or FORWARDREF
  • ValueError when eval_str=true is combined with a format other than VALUE
  • NotImplementedError surfaced if an annotate function rejects the requested format and no fallback succeeds
  • Unresolvable target reference (module/class/function not found) reported as a lookup error
  • Arbitrary exceptions from user-supplied annotate functions, including infinite loops or side effects

Ranked use cases

  1. Framework/DI container resolving type hints for classes and functions at registration time using FORWARDREF to tolerate not-yet-defined names
  2. Documentation and API-reference generators rendering annotations as source-like strings via STRING format
  3. Metaclass tooling that inspects class-body annotations during class creation using get_annotate_from_class_namespace and call_annotate_function
  4. Static-analysis and linting tools that need reliable annotation retrieval across modules, classes, and callables
  5. Serialization/schema generators (e.g. dataclass or TypedDict to JSON Schema) that consume resolved annotation values

Source digest sha256:7d473defbae0b6d85b41cca023807820774cb6314acefb3b091df297f378b81b

argparse

Command-line interface libraries

Python documentation

Build an argparse.ArgumentParser from a declarative JSON specification and parse a supplied argv list into a plain dict, without touching sys.argv or exiting the process.

APIs

  • argparse.ArgumentParser
  • ArgumentParser.add_argument
  • ArgumentParser.parse_args
  • argparse.Namespace
  • argparse.ArgumentError

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"prog":{"type":"string"},"description":{"type":"string"},"epilog":{"type":"string"},"add_help":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"allow_abbrev":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"exit_on_error":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"arguments":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name_or_flags":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":1},"action":{"type":"string"},"nargs":{"type":["integer","string"]},"const":{},"default":{},"type":{"type":"string","enum":["str","int","float"]},"choices":{"type":"array"},"required":{"type":"boolean"},"help":{"type":"string"},"metavar":{"type":"string"},"dest":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name_or_flags"]}},"argv":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["arguments","argv"]}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"values":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true},"error":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"kind":{"type":"string"},"message":{"type":"string"}},"required":["kind","message"]}},"required":["ok","values","error"]}

Effects Pure in-memory construction and parsing; no process exit, no sys.argv access, no filesystem or network I/O. Help/usage text is not printed; only structured results are returned.

Constraints Requires Python 3.2+ for argparse; exit_on_error requires 3.9+; suggest_on_error and color are 3.14+ and are not exposed here. Only str/int/float converters are supported to keep error handling bounded. No subparsers, FileType, fromfile_prefix_chars, or custom Action classes in this bounded operation.

Failure modes

  • Invalid specification: conflicting option strings raise ArgumentError during add_argument (unless conflict_handler resolves them).
  • Invalid specification: unsupported action, nargs, or type name is rejected before parsing.
  • Parse failure: missing required argument, unrecognized argument, or invalid choice/type conversion raises ArgumentError when exit_on_error is False.
  • Type conversion errors from int/float converters are surfaced as ArgumentError rather than raw ValueError.
  • argv containing non-string elements is rejected as a specification/input error.

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders generating CLI front-ends for SideFX estate tools from declarative argument specs.
  2. Validating and normalizing user-supplied argument lists in tests without invoking sys.exit.
  3. Wrapping existing scripts to expose typed, documented parameters to orchestration layers.
  4. Producing structured parse results for downstream job configuration in pipeline tooling.
  5. Safely parsing untrusted argv fragments in sandboxed or embedded contexts where process exit is unacceptable.

array

Data Types

Python documentation

array.pack_numeric: construct a typed array from a list of numeric values and return its machine-value byte representation plus metadata (typecode, itemsize, element count, byte length).

APIs

  • array.array(typecode[, initializer])
  • array.array.tobytes()
  • array.array.itemsize
  • array.array.typecode
  • array.typecodes

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"typecode":{"type":"string","description":"Single-character (or \u0027Zf\u0027/\u0027Zd\u0027) array type code; must be a member of array.typecodes."},"values":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["integer","number"]},"description":"Numeric values to store; must be coercible to the element type of typecode."},"byteOrder":{"type":"string","enum":["native","swapped"],"default":"native","description":"If \u0027swapped\u0027, apply byteswap() before serializing."}},"required":["typecode","values"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

atexit

Python Runtime Services

Python documentation

Register a named, argument-bound exit handler within the current interpreter and return a stable registration token, without executing the handler at registration time.

APIs

  • atexit.register(func, *args, **kwargs) — registers func as an exit handler, passing stored positional/keyword arguments at interpreter shutdown, and returns func (enabling decorator use); used to bind the handler and its arguments.
  • atexit.unregister(func) — removes all occurrences of func from the exit-handler stack using == equality; used to support idempotent rollback of a registration by token.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"handlerName":{"type":"string","description":"Logical name identifying the handler for later reference"},"args":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Positional arguments forwarded to the handler at exit"},"kwargs":{"type":"object","description":"Keyword arguments forwarded to the handler at exit"},"allowDuplicate":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to permit registering the same handler more than once"}},"required":["handlerName"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"registered":{"type":"boolean"},"token":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque token usable to unregister the handler"},"handlerName":{"type":"string"},"duplicate":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if an equivalent registration already existed"}},"required":["registered","token","handlerName"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Mutates the current interpreter's exit-handler stack only; no handler code runs at registration time. Handlers execute in reverse registration order at normal interpreter shutdown (sys.exit, main module completion, or interpreter close). No effect on signal-killed processes, fatal internal errors, or os._exit().

Constraints Per-interpreter scope: registrations affect only the calling interpreter (subinterpreters isolated since 3.7). Registration/unregistration from within a cleanup function is undefined. Handlers must tolerate other handlers running arbitrary Python code afterward. No new threads or forks from handlers (3.12+). Not invoked on unhandled signals, fatal errors, or os._exit().

Failure modes

  • Handler name not resolvable to a callable in the current interpreter context
  • Duplicate registration rejected when allowDuplicate is false
  • Registration attempted from within an exit handler (undefined behavior per docs)
  • Unregister called with a token whose handler was already removed (silently no-op per docs)
  • Handler raising an exception at shutdown: traceback printed and last exception re-raised after all handlers run
  • RuntimeError if the handler attempts to start a thread or os.fork() (Python 3.12+)

Ranked use cases

  1. Flush and persist in-memory counters or caches to a file at clean interpreter shutdown (as in the documented counterfile example).
  2. Register ordered teardown of lower-level resources (sockets, temp files, locks) so they are released after higher-level modules clean up.
  3. Provide decorator-style registration of no-argument cleanup functions for library authors.
  4. Support idempotent unregistration of handlers by token to avoid duplicate cleanup in long-lived interpreters.
  5. Isolate per-subinterpreter cleanup stacks for embedded or concurrent.interpreters workloads.

Internet Data Handling

Python documentation

Compute a CRC-32 checksum over a bounded byte payload, optionally chained from a prior CRC value, and return the unsigned 32-bit result as an integer plus a zero-padded lowercase hex string.

APIs

  • binascii.crc32(data[, value]) — computes the unsigned 32-bit CRC-32 (ZIP-consistent) checksum of a bytes-like payload, accepting an optional initial CRC value to support incremental/chained computation; this is the sole real API the operation relies on.
  • binascii.Error — the module's exception type, referenced as the error class surfaced when input validation fails at the binding boundary.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bytes representing the payload to checksum; decoded to a bytes-like object before being passed to binascii.crc32."},"initialCrc":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":4294967295,"description":"Optional prior CRC-32 value to chain from; defaults to 0."}},"required":["data"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"crc":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":4294967295,"description":"Unsigned 32-bit CRC-32 result."},"hex":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[0-9a-f]{8}$","description":"Zero-padded lowercase 8-character hex representation of crc."},"byteLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of payload bytes checksummed."}},"required":["crc","hex","byteLength"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation with no side effects: no filesystem, network, environment, or global state is read or modified. The operation is deterministic and idempotent for identical inputs.

Constraints Requires a CPython runtime exposing the binascii module (present in standard CPython builds; not guaranteed on all workers or alternative interpreters). Payload size must be bounded by the caller's configured limit. The CRC-32 algorithm is a checksum, not a cryptographic hash, and must not be used for integrity against adversarial tampering. No installation, availability, or execution is claimed by this proposal.

Failure modes

  • Invalid base64 in 'data' — decoding fails before binascii.crc32 is invoked; surfaced as a validation error.
  • 'data' missing or not a string — schema validation error.
  • 'initialCrc' out of the 0..2**32-1 range or non-integer — schema validation error.
  • Payload exceeding the configured maximum size — rejected as a bounds violation.
  • Unexpected TypeError from binascii.crc32 if the decoded object is not bytes-like — surfaced as binascii.Error at the binding boundary.

Ranked use cases

  1. Incremental ZIP/archive integrity verification: chain crc32 across streamed chunks to validate member checksums without buffering whole files.
  2. Content-addressed deduplication keys for binary blobs where a fast non-cryptographic fingerprint suffices.
  3. Wire-protocol frame validation: compute and compare CRC-32 trailers on received binary frames.
  4. Data-pipeline change detection: cheaply detect whether serialized records changed between runs.
  5. Test-fixture and golden-file verification: assert stable checksums of generated binary artifacts in CI.

Data Types

Python documentation

bisect_locate_insertion_point: given a sorted sequence of comparable values (or records plus a key field), a target value, and optional lo/hi bounds, return the insertion index that maintains sorted order, using left (before equal entries) or right (after equal entries) semantics.

APIs

  • bisect.bisect_left(a, x, lo=0, hi=len(a), *, key=None)
  • bisect.bisect_right(a, x, lo=0, hi=len(a), *, key=None)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"sequence":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Sorted sequence of comparable elements (or records when key is given)."},"target":{"description":"Value to locate insertion point for; compared via __lt__ only."},"side":{"type":"string","enum":["left","right"],"default":"left"},"lo":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":0},"hi":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Exclusive upper bound; defaults to len(sequence)."},"keyField":{"type":["string","null"],"default":null,"description":"If set, elements are records and this field is used as the comparison key; target is compared directly against extracted keys."}},"required":["sequence","target"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"index":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Insertion point suitable for list.insert(index, target)."},"side":{"type":"string","enum":["left","right"]},"lo":{"type":"integer"},"hi":{"type":"integer"},"length":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["index","side","lo","hi","length"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure read-only computation; no mutation of the input sequence, no I/O, no global state changes. The returned index is advisory and only valid against the same sequence state.

Constraints Not thread-safe per documentation: concurrent mutation of the sequence during the call yields undefined results. Comparison uses only __lt__ (never __eq__). Search is O(log n) but any subsequent insertion is O(n). key function results are not cached across calls. Requires Python 3.10+ for the key parameter.

Failure modes

  • TypeError when elements or target are not mutually orderable via __lt__
  • ValueError when lo or hi is out of range or lo > hi
  • KeyError/AttributeError when keyField is missing on a record
  • Incorrect results if the input sequence is not actually sorted
  • Undefined behavior if the sequence is mutated concurrently by another thread
  • Non-deterministic results if keyField extraction is inconsistent across elements

Ranked use cases

  1. Maintaining sorted record tables (e.g., namedtuple/row records) by computing insertion points before list.insert, avoiding full re-sorts
  2. Numeric breakpoint/grade lookups (e.g., mapping scores to letter grades via bisect_right over ordered thresholds)
  3. Range and boundary queries over sorted data (find_lt/find_le/find_gt/find_ge patterns) for capability builders
  4. Precomputed-key index search to avoid repeated expensive key extraction on large sorted datasets
  5. Partitioning sorted event or timestamp logs into left/right slices around a pivot for downstream processing

  • bz2.decompress(data) — decompresses a bytes-like bzip2 stream (including multi-stream concatenations) back to bytes; used as the verification step.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"dataBase64":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded raw bytes to compress (bounded payload)."},"compressLevel":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":9,"default":9,"description":"bzip2 compression level passed to bz2.compress."}},"required":["dataBase64"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"compressedBase64":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bzip2-compressed bytes."},"inputBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"compressedBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"ratio":{"type":"number","description":"inputBytes / compressedBytes, or null when compressedBytes is 0."},"roundTripEqual":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if bz2.decompress(compressed) equals the original input bytes."}},"required":["compressedBase64","inputBytes","compressedBytes","ratio","roundTripEqual"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints Requires a CPython build with the optional bz2 module compiled in; availability is not guaranteed and must be probed at runtime. BZ2File is documented as thread-unsafe for concurrent readers/writers, so this operation avoids shared file objects and uses only one-shot functions on isolated buffers. Payload size must be bounded by the caller. No installation or execution is claimed here.

  • Invalid base64 in dataBase64 (decode error).
  • compressLevel outside 1..9 or non-integer (ValueError/TypeError from bz2.compress).
  • Payload exceeds configured size bound (rejected before compression).
  • bz2 module not present in the interpreter (optional module missing) — ImportError.
  • Decompression of the produced stream fails (OSError/EOFError) indicating an internal inconsistency.
  • Memory exhaustion on very large payloads during compress/decompress.

Ranked use cases

  1. Round-trip integrity check for bzip2 payloads before storing or transmitting compressed artifacts.
  2. Compression-ratio benchmarking across compressLevel values for a given data class.
  3. Pre-flight validation of bzip2 support and correctness in a target interpreter environment.
  4. Generating deterministic compressed fixtures for tests of downstream decompression consumers.
  5. Sanity-checking data pipelines that must preserve byte-exact content through bzip2 compression.

Command-line interface libraries

Python documentation

Dispatch a single command line through a Cmd subclass instance without entering the interactive loop: construct the subclass with supplied stdin/stdout, set use_rawinput to False, then call onecmd(line) once and capture the returned stop flag plus captured output.

APIs

  • cmd.Cmd.onecmd(line) — interprets a single line as if typed at the prompt and returns the stop flag from the dispatched do_* method or default()
  • cmd.Cmd.__init__(completekey, stdin, stdout) — binds the interpreter to provided file objects and completion key
  • cmd.Cmd.use_rawinput — instance flag that must be set False so the supplied stdin is honored
  • cmd.Cmd.default(line) — fallback invoked for unrecognized command prefixes
  • cmd.Cmd.precmd(line) / cmd.Cmd.postcmd(stop, line) — hooks that may rewrite the line and adjust the stop flag

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"line":{"type":"string","description":"Single command line to dispatch, without trailing newline"},"completekey":{"type":["string","null"],"default":"tab"},"use_rawinput":{"type":"boolean","default":false}},"required":["line"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"stop":{"type":"boolean","description":"Truthiness of the value returned by onecmd"},"returnValue":{"type":["string","number","boolean","null"],"description":"JSON-safe rendering of the do_* return value"},"stdout":{"type":"string","description":"Text written to the captured stdout during dispatch"},"dispatched":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether a do_* method matched the command prefix"}},"required":["stop","stdout","dispatched"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-process dispatch: no network, filesystem or subprocess effects unless the user's do_* methods perform them. Output is captured via an in-memory stdout substitute; no installation, availability or execution on any worker is claimed.

Constraints Requires a user-defined Cmd subclass; base Cmd is not useful standalone. Interactive cmdloop, readline history and tab completion are out of scope for this bounded single-line operation. Behavior of do_shell ('!') and do_help ('?') depends on subclass definitions. Platform differences in readline backend (editline vs GNU readline) affect completekey handling only.

Failure modes

  • Unknown command prefix routes to default(), which prints an error and returns None; dispatched is false
  • do_* method raises an exception that propagates out of onecmd and must be surfaced as an error result
  • Non-JSON-serializable return value from do_* cannot be represented in returnValue
  • Supplied stdin ignored if use_rawinput remains True
  • readline unavailable or completekey invalid for the active backend; completion silently disabled
  • Empty line triggers emptyline() which may repeat the last command, producing unexpected dispatch

Ranked use cases

  1. Test harnesses that drive a Cmd-based shell one command at a time and assert on stop flags and output
  2. Administrative tool prototypes needing scripted, non-interactive replay of recorded command files via cmdqueue
  3. Record/playback facilities that validate each recorded line through onecmd before bulk playback
  4. Capability builders wrapping legacy Cmd shells behind a structured request/response interface
  5. Regression testing of do_* dispatch, default() fallback and precmd/postcmd hook behavior

codeop

Custom Python Interpreters

Python documentation

Classify a single line of Python source as COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE, or INVALID using codeop.compile_command, without executing it, to decide whether a REPL-style prompt should be '>>>' or '...' or whether to report a syntax error.

APIs

  • codeop.compile_command(source, filename='', symbol='single') — attempts to compile source and returns a code object if valid, None if source is a valid prefix of a statement (incomplete), and raises SyntaxError/OverflowError/ValueError otherwise; used as the core classifier.
  • codeop.CommandCompiler — callable with compile_command-compatible signature that remembers __future__ statements across calls; noted as the stateful alternative for multi-line sessions.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"source":{"type":"string","description":"Python source text to classify"},"filename":{"type":"string","default":"\u003Cinput\u003E","description":"Filename attribute for the compiled code object"},"symbol":{"type":"string","enum":["single","exec","eval"],"default":"single","description":"Compilation mode"}},"required":["source"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string","enum":["COMPLETE","INCOMPLETE","INVALID"]},"errorType":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Exception class name when INVALID, else null"},"errorMessage":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Exception message when INVALID, else null"}},"required":["status","errorType","errorMessage"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation: compiles source in memory to a code object that is discarded; no execution of the source, no filesystem, network, or global-state changes. The stateless compile_command path does not persist __future__ state; a CommandCompiler-based variant would hold per-instance state only.

Constraints Requires a CPython-compatible interpreter with the codeop module present; behavior of compile_command depends on the running interpreter version's parser and grammar. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed. Not a sandbox: classification does not guarantee the source is safe to execute. The 'single' symbol mode is intended for interactive-style input and may differ from 'exec'/'eval' semantics.

Failure modes

  • SyntaxError raised by compile_command for invalid syntax — mapped to INVALID with errorType 'SyntaxError'.
  • OverflowError or ValueError raised for invalid literals — mapped to INVALID with the corresponding errorType.
  • ValueError raised when symbol is not one of 'single', 'exec', 'eval' — surfaced as a contract violation rather than a classification.
  • Non-string source (e.g. bytes or None) — rejected by input validation before calling the API.
  • Documented parser caveat: parsing may succeed before end of source, so trailing garbage after certain constructs may be silently ignored, yielding COMPLETE when a stricter check would fail.

Ranked use cases

  1. Driving REPL prompt selection ('>>>' vs '...') in an interactive Python console UI.
  2. Validating and gating user-entered code snippets in a notebook or editor before submission.
  3. Incrementally assembling multi-line statements from streamed input in a chat or terminal front end.
  4. Pre-flight syntax checking of generated code in an LLM code-generation pipeline before execution.
  5. Building a stateful interpreter session using CommandCompiler to honor __future__ imports across inputs.

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"success":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if all considered files compiled successfully"},"dir":{"type":"string"},"compiled":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Count of .py files successfully byte-compiled"},"skipped":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Count of files skipped by rx or symlink limits"},"failed":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Count of files that failed to compile"},"errors":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"},"message":{"type":"string"}},"required":["path","message"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["success","dir","compiled","skipped","failed","errors"],"additionalProperties":false}

Generated caches are only useful at runtime if sys.pycache_prefix matches the value used at compile time. ddir is mutually exclusive with stripdir/prependdir.   4. Producing reproducible hash-based .pyc files (checked-hash) for SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-driven reproducible builds
  5. Excluding vendored or VCS directories (e.g., .svn, .git) from compilation via the rx regex filter

Enumerate the submodules exposed by the concurrent package (concurrent.futures, concurrent.interpreters) as a bounded, read-only capability inventory for the SideFX estate, without importing or executing them.

APIs

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"package":{"type":"string","const":"concurrent"},"submodules":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","enum":["concurrent.futures","concurrent.interpreters"]},"minItems":1,"maxItems":2},"includeOrigin":{"type":"boolean","default":false}},"required":["package","submodules"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only. No modules are imported, no threads, processes, or interpreters are created, and no files are written. The only observable effect is a metadata lookup via importlib.util.find_spec, which may populate sys.modules caches for parent packages in the calling process; this is documented as a caveat, not a guarantee.

Constraints Design proposal only; not installed, not available on any worker, and not executed. Behavior depends on the interpreter's import system and sys.path; results may differ across Python versions (concurrent.interpreters is documented for 3.15). Must not be used to infer runtime capability, only documented module presence. No network, no subprocess, no filesystem writes. Platform-neutral in principle but unverified on any platform.

  • InvalidArgument: 'package' is not the literal 'concurrent'
  • InvalidArgument: 'submodules' is empty, exceeds two entries, or contains a name outside the documented set
  • InvalidArgument: unknown or extra properties present (additionalProperties=false)
  • SpecLookupError: importlib.util.find_spec raises (e.g. ValueError for malformed names, ImportError for parent package issues) — surfaced as a per-entry error rather than aborting the whole call
  • PartialResult: some submodules resolve and others do not; each entry reports found=false independently

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability inventory: report which documented concurrent submodules a given interpreter advertises, to gate later design work on concurrent.futures or concurrent.interpreters.
  2. Pre-flight validation for capability builders: confirm a target interpreter exposes concurrent.futures before designing task-launching bindings around it.
  3. Documentation-to-runtime drift detection: compare the documented submodule list against what find_spec resolves, flagging mismatches for review.
  4. Dependency manifest generation: emit a machine-readable list of concurrent submodules with origins for downstream tooling, without importing them.
  5. Safety audit: verify that probing the concurrent package performs no imports or execution, supporting least-privilege review of provider bindings.

concurrent.futures

Concurrent Execution

Python documentation

bounded_thread_pool_map: run a caller-supplied callable over a bounded list of argument tuples on a ThreadPoolExecutor with a fixed max_workers, a per-future timeout, and a hard cap on task count, returning per-task outcomes (value or error) without exposing Future objects.

APIs

  • concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor (constructor with max_workers, thread_name_prefix, initializer, initargs) — creates the bounded worker pool used to execute tasks
  • concurrent.futures.Executor.submit(fn, *args, **kwargs) — schedules each callable and returns a Future per task
  • concurrent.futures.Future.result(timeout=None) — retrieves each task's return value or re-raises its exception, bounded by timeout
  • concurrent.futures.as_completed(fs, timeout=None) — yields futures as they complete so results are collected in completion order
  • concurrent.futures.Executor.shutdown(wait=True, cancel_futures=False) — releases pool resources deterministically after the bounded batch

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"callable_ref":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path of a picklable-free, importable callable to invoke per task"},"tasks":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{}},"minItems":1,"maxItems":256,"description":"List of positional-argument tuples, one per task"},"max_workers":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":32},"timeout_seconds":{"type":["number","null"],"minimum":0},"thread_name_prefix":{"type":"string","default":""}},"required":["callable_ref","tasks","max_workers"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"results":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"index":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"status":{"type":"string","enum":["ok","error","timeout","cancelled"]},"value":{},"error_type":{"type":["string","null"]},"error_message":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["index","status"],"additionalProperties":false}},"completed_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"failed_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"timed_out_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["results","completed_count","failed_count","timed_out_count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Spawns up to max_workers threads within the calling process; executes the named callable with caller-supplied arguments; performs no filesystem, network or subprocess side effects itself (any such effects come solely from the callable); joins all worker threads before returning; does not persist state between calls.

Constraints Not available on WASI/WebAssembly platforms. Runs only in-process threads (no process or interpreter isolation, so the GIL applies). Callable must be importable by dotted path and arguments must be JSON-representable. Task count capped at 256 and max_workers capped at 32 to bound resource use. Timeout applies per Future.result call, not to the whole batch. Not suitable for long-running tasks because threads are joined at interpreter exit. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • callable_ref cannot be imported or is not callable -> validation error before any task is submitted
  • tasks empty or exceeding maxItems cap -> validation error
  • max_workers out of range (<=0 or >32) -> validation error
  • a task raises an exception -> captured per-task as status 'error' with error_type and error_message; batch continues
  • Future.result raises TimeoutError for a task -> recorded as status 'timeout'
  • Future cancelled before running (e.g. shutdown with cancel_futures) -> recorded as status 'cancelled'
  • worker initializer raises -> BrokenThreadPool surfaces as a batch-level failure
  • nested submission from within a task that waits on another future can deadlock the pool -> documented hazard, not auto-detected
  • interpreter exit blocked until all worker threads join -> long-running tasks delay process exit

Ranked use cases

  1. Bounded fan-out of I/O-bound lookups (e.g. fetching many URLs or records) with per-task timeout and error capture
  2. Parallelizing independent pure computations over a fixed argument list while keeping worker count and task count capped
  3. Batch validation or transformation of many small inputs where per-item failures must be reported without aborting the batch
  4. Overlapping slow external calls (database, RPC) in a capability pipeline with deterministic shutdown and no leaked threads
  5. Prototyping map-style parallelism for capability builders before deciding whether process or interpreter isolation is needed

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"callableRef":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path of the function to invoke inside the new interpreter, e.g. \u0027mymod.compute\u0027."},"args":{"type":"array","description":"Positional arguments; each must be picklable or a supported shared type.","items":{}},"kwargs":{"type":"object","description":"Keyword arguments; values must be picklable or a supported shared type.","additionalProperties":true},"mainNamespace":{"type":"object","description":"Objects to bind into the interpreter\u0027s __main__ via prepare_main before the call.","additionalProperties":true},"timeoutSeconds":{"type":"number","description":"Optional advisory timeout for the caller; not enforced by the interpreter itself."}},"required":["callableRef"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"result":{"description":"Return value of the call, copied back to the caller interpreter."},"error":{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["ExecutionFailed","NotShareableError","InterpreterNotFoundError","InterpreterError"]},"message":{"type":"string"},"excinfo":{"type":["object","null"],"description":"Snapshot from ExecutionFailed.excinfo when applicable."}},"required":["kind","message"],"additionalProperties":false},"interpreterId":{"type":"integer","description":"ID of the interpreter that was created and closed."}},"required":["ok","interpreterId"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Creates and finalizes a new isolated interpreter in the current process; binds objects into that interpreter's __main__; executes the callable in the current thread; copies the result back via pickle or shared-type transfer. Interpreters are isolated by default and do not start implicit threads; concurrency requires combining with threads (e.g. call_in_thread or InterpreterPoolExecutor). Isolation is best-effort, not a security boundary. Not all PyPI extension modules support multiple interpreters. Mutable objects are copied, not shared, except memoryview and Queue. Requires Python 3.14+ (module added in 3.14).

  • ExecutionFailed when the target callable raises an uncaught exception; excinfo carries a basic snapshot.
  • InterpreterNotFoundError if the created interpreter is finalized before the call completes.
  • InterpreterError for other interpreter-related failures (e.g. binding into __main__ fails).
  • ImportError/AttributeError inside the interpreter when callableRef cannot be resolved.
  • Timeout is advisory only; the operation does not itself interrupt a long-running call.

Ranked use cases

  1. Sandboxed execution of untrusted-ish plugin code with a fresh import state and builtins per call.
  2. Parallel CPU-bound batch jobs by pairing created interpreters with threads to bypass the GIL.
  3. Actor/CSP-style worker design using create_queue for message passing between isolated interpreters.
  4. Test harness that runs a function in a clean interpreter to detect global-state leakage or import side effects.
  5. Library isolation for conflicting dependency versions or module-level state across logical components.

  2. Static analysis and review tooling that verifies cleanup ordering and suppression semantics before code runs.

  4. Feeding deterministic screen-state fixtures to capability builders that need to reason about rendered terminal output

Naive vs aware distinction is preserved and reported via isAware; no implicit local-time assumption is made. Platform C localtime()/gmtime() are not used, so no 1970-2038 restriction applies. total_seconds()-style precision loss is avoided by reporting integer offset seconds.   3. Extracting ISO week-year/week/weekday for calendar-based reporting and partitioning without re-parsing

dbm_probe: given a filesystem path, report whether a DBM-family database exists there, which backend module dbm.whichdb() identifies for it, and whether the path is readable — without opening the database for read/write or mutating it.

APIs

  • dbm.whichdb(filename) — returns None if the file is unreadable or missing, '' if the format cannot be guessed, or a module name string such as 'dbm.gnu' or 'dbm.ndbm'; this is the sole API invoked by the operation
  • dbm.error — tuple of backend exceptions, referenced only to classify error reporting (not raised by whichdb)
  • dbm.open(file, flag='r', mode=0o666) — documented for context only; NOT invoked by this bounded operation

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path (path-like) to the candidate DBM database file or basename"},"followSymlinks":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Whether symlinks are resolved before probing"}},"required":["path"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"exists":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if the path is present and readable"},"backend":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["dbm.sqlite3","dbm.gnu","dbm.ndbm","dbm.dumb","",null],"description":"Module name reported by dbm.whichdb(); \u0027\u0027 means format unrecognized, null means missing/unreadable"},"recognized":{"type":"boolean","description":"True only when backend is a non-empty module name"},"path":{"type":"string","description":"Echo of the resolved path that was probed"}},"required":["exists","backend","recognized","path"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only. Performs a filesystem stat/read probe via dbm.whichdb(); creates, opens for writing, locks, reorganizes, or syncs nothing. No database file is modified and no backend module is imported beyond what whichdb itself requires.

Constraints Unix-oriented; dbm.gnu and dbm.ndbm are documented as unavailable on Android, iOS and WASI, and dbm.sqlite3 is unavailable on WASI. dbm.ndbm on macOS has an undocumented value-size limitation that can corrupt files, so probing must never be followed by blind writes. dbm.dumb does not support concurrent read/write access. whichdb's answer is a guess and must not be treated as a guarantee of openability. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • Path does not exist or is unreadable: whichdb returns None; operation reports exists=false, backend=null, recognized=false (not an exception)
  • File exists but format is not a known DBM variant: whichdb returns ''; operation reports exists=true, backend='', recognized=false
  • Permission denied on parent directory or file: surfaced as exists=false with backend=null; caller must distinguish via separate stat if needed
  • Non-path-like input (e.g. integer): TypeError from path coercion
  • Backend-specific detection ambiguity: whichdb may misidentify a corrupt or truncated file; result is advisory only
  • Platform where a given backend is unavailable (e.g. dbm.gnu on Android/iOS/WASI): whichdb may still name it, but the operation does not verify importability

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight backend detection before choosing an open flag, so a capability builder can decide whether to open with 'r', 'w', 'c' or 'n' without risking accidental creation or truncation
  2. Inventory and classification of legacy DBM files (gnu/ndbm/dumb/sqlite3) across a filesystem for migration planning toward dbm.sqlite3
  3. Guarding shelve-style workflows by confirming the underlying dbm format before handing the path to shelve.open
  4. Diagnostics for corrupt or unrecognized database files by distinguishing 'missing' (None) from 'unknown format' ('')
  5. Routing decisions in a persistence layer that must pick a backend-specific code path (e.g. reorganize() availability differs across dbm.sqlite3, dbm.gnu and dbm.dumb)

dbm.dumb

Data Persistence

Python documentation

dbm.dumb.open(filename, flag='c', mode=0o666) — open a portable pure-Python DBM database at basename filename (creating filename.dat and filename.dir when needed) and return a dict-like handle supporting get/set/delete, keys(), get(), setdefault(), clear(), close(), sync() and reorganize(), usable as a closing context manager.

APIs

  • dbm.dumb.open(filename, flag='c', mode=0o666) — opens/creates the portable database and returns the dumbdbm mapping object
  • dumbdbm.sync() — flushes the on-disk .dir and .dat files
  • dumbdbm.reorganize() — compacts the database to reclaim space from deletions
  • dumbdbm.close() — closes the database handle
  • dbm.whichdb(filename) — identifies which dbm backend a file belongs to (used to confirm dbm.dumb ownership)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Basename of the database file without .dat/.dir extensions"},"flag":{"type":"string","enum":["r","w","c","n"],"default":"c"},"mode":{"type":"integer","default":438,"description":"Unix file access mode used only when creating"}},"required":["filename"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"handle":{"type":"object","description":"Opaque dumbdbm mapping handle; not serializable"},"filename":{"type":"string"},"flag":{"type":"string"},"created":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if new .dat/.dir files were created"},"files":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Paths of the .dat and .dir files backing the database"}},"required":["handle","filename","flag","created","files"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Creates or modifies filename.dat and filename.dir on the local filesystem; writes are buffered until sync()/close(); reorganize() rewrites the database in place to reclaim deleted space (no additional free disk space required for dbm.dumb); no network or external library involvement.

Constraints Pure-Python implementation requiring no external library; intended as a last-resort fallback for dbm, not written for speed; keys and values are stored as bytes and always returned as bytes; keys accept str and bytes only (bytearray allowed as value, not key); keys() and items() return lists; setdefault() requires two arguments; no concurrent read/write access; reorganize() added in 3.15; filename accepts path-like objects since 3.11; flag 'n' always creates a new empty database since 3.5; read-only open with 'r' since 3.8.

Failure modes

  • dbm.dumb.error raised on dbm.dumb-specific I/O errors
  • KeyError raised for general mapping errors such as missing keys
  • FileNotFoundError/OSError when flag is 'r' or 'w' and the database does not exist (no creation in those modes)
  • TypeError when a non-str/bytes key is supplied, or when bytearray is used as a key (bytearray is acceptable only as a value)
  • Interpreter crash possible when loading a database with a sufficiently large/complex entry due to AST compiler stack depth limits
  • Corruption or inconsistent state if concurrent read/write access occurs (dbm.dumb does not support concurrent read/write; multiple simultaneous readers are safe)
  • PermissionError when mode/file permissions prevent creation or writing

Ranked use cases

  1. Fallback persistence layer for shelve/dbm when no native backend (dbm.gnu, dbm.ndbm, dbm.sqlite3) is available
  2. Portable key-value cache or lookup store in constrained or cross-platform environments without external DBM libraries
  3. Small on-disk configuration/metadata store for tools that must run on any Python installation
  4. Test fixture backend for exercising dbm/shelve code paths without native dependencies
  5. Space reclamation of long-lived key-value stores via reorganize() after heavy deletion workloads

Open a GDBM database read-only and enumerate all keys via firstkey/nextkey traversal, returning keys and values as base64-encoded bytes without loading a full key list into memory.

  • dbm.gnu.open(filename, flag='r', mode=0o666, /)
  • gdbm.firstkey()
  • gdbm.nextkey(key)
  • gdbm.close()

  • dbm.gnu.open_flags

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Path to the GDBM database file"},"maxEntries":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Maximum number of key/value pairs to return"},"includeValues":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Whether to fetch and return values alongside keys"}},"required":["filename"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"entries":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"keyB64":{"type":"string"},"valueB64":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["keyB64","valueB64"],"additionalProperties":false}},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"count":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["entries","truncated","count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only: opens the database with flag 'r', performs no writes, no reorganization, and no sync; closes the handle on completion. No filesystem mutation occurs.

Constraints Unix only; not available on Android, iOS, or WASI. Requires the GDBM library to be present. Traversal order follows GDBM internal hash order, not sorted order. Keys and values are always returned as bytes. The operation is bounded by maxEntries to avoid unbounded memory use.

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders enumerating keys of an existing GDBM cache file to inspect contents without loading all keys into memory
  2. Diagnostic tooling that dumps GDBM database entries as base64 for offline analysis
  3. Migration helpers that read GDBM key/value pairs to transfer into another backend
  4. Audit/inventory scripts that count and sample entries in GDBM files on Unix hosts
  5. Test fixtures that verify GDBM database contents after a producer writes them

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Basename of the NDBM database file without .dir/.pag extensions"},"key":{"type":"string","description":"Key to look up; str is accepted and implicitly encoded to bytes"},"default":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional fallback returned when key is absent; null means raise KeyError"}},"required":["filename","key"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"found":{"type":"boolean"},"value":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Base64-encoded bytes value, or null when not found"},"library":{"type":"string","description":"Value of dbm.ndbm.library for the active implementation"}},"required":["found","value","library"],"additionalProperties":false}

  2. Capability builders exposing a bounded, non-mutating get operation over existing Unix NDBM stores

decimal

Numeric and Mathematical Modules

Python documentation

quantize_decimal: round a decimal value to a fixed exponent (fixed number of decimal places) under an explicit, caller-supplied precision/rounding context, returning the rounded value plus the resulting context flags, without mutating the thread's current context.

APIs

  • decimal.Decimal.quantize(exp, rounding=None, context=None)
  • decimal.Context(prec, rounding, Emin, Emax, capitals, clamp, flags, traps)
  • decimal.localcontext(ctx=None, **kwargs)
  • decimal.getcontext()

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"value":{"type":"string","description":"Decimal numeric string per the module\u0027s numeric-string grammar (sign, digits, optional exponent, Infinity/NaN)."},"exponent":{"type":"string","description":"Target exponent as a Decimal string, e.g. \u00270.01\u0027 or \u00271.\u0027."},"prec":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Context precision for the operation."},"rounding":{"type":"string","enum":["ROUND_CEILING","ROUND_DOWN","ROUND_FLOOR","ROUND_HALF_DOWN","ROUND_HALF_EVEN","ROUND_HALF_UP","ROUND_UP","ROUND_05UP"],"description":"Rounding mode; defaults to context rounding if omitted."}},"required":["value","exponent","prec"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"result":{"type":"string","description":"Quantized Decimal rendered as a string."},"exponent":{"type":"integer","description":"Resulting exponent of the quantized value."},"flags":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Context signal flags raised during the operation (e.g. Inexact, Rounded, InvalidOperation)."},"is_finite":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["result","exponent","flags","is_finite"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation. The operation runs inside a localcontext() copy so the thread's current context, its flags and traps are left unchanged; no I/O, no filesystem or network access, no global state mutation. Returned flags reflect only this operation.

Constraints Requires CPython's decimal module (pure-Python or _decimal C accelerator); behavior of flags/traps may differ slightly between implementations. Precision must be within [1, MAX_PREC]; exponent limits within [MIN_EMIN, MAX_EMAX]. quantize never signals Underflow. No installation, availability or execution is claimed; this is a design proposal only.

Failure modes

  • InvalidOperation: malformed input string, or coefficient length after quantize exceeds context precision
  • InvalidOperation: resulting exponent greater than Emax or less than Etiny()
  • InvalidOperation: signaling NaN operand or infinity where quantize cannot produce a finite result
  • ValueError/TypeError: exponent argument not a valid Decimal string or prec out of allowed range
  • FloatOperation: if a float is accidentally supplied where a Decimal string is required and the trap is enabled

Ranked use cases

  1. Monetary rounding: quantize invoice/ledger amounts to a fixed number of minor units (e.g. '0.01') with an explicit rounding mode for accounting invariants.
  2. Tax and interest computation: apply a caller-specified precision and ROUND_HALF_EVEN to avoid binary-float drift in financial totals.
  3. Unit-price normalization: standardize prices to a fixed exponent before aggregation so sums preserve significant trailing zeros.
  4. Scientific/measurement reporting: round measured values to a requested decimal place while capturing Inexact/Rounded flags for audit.
  5. Deterministic test fixtures: produce reproducible rounded decimal outputs under a pinned context for regression testing of numeric pipelines.

{"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Lines of the first sequence (newline-terminated recommended)"},"b":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Lines of the second sequence"},"fromfile":{"type":"string","default":""},"tofile":{"type":"string","default":""},"fromfiledate":{"type":"string","default":""},"tofiledate":{"type":"string","default":""},"n":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":3},"lineterm":{"type":"string","default":"\n"}},"required":["a","b"],"additionalProperties":false}

faulthandler

Debugging and profiling

Python documentation

dump_current_thread_traceback_to_file: capture a bounded, signal-safe-style snapshot of the current thread's Python traceback into a caller-supplied file object (or file descriptor), with an explicit frame/thread cap, without installing any fault handlers or timers.

APIs

  • faulthandler.dump_traceback(file, all_threads=False, max_threads=...)
  • faulthandler.is_enabled()

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"file":{"type":["object","integer"],"description":"Writable file-like object or open file descriptor to receive the dump"},"all_threads":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, dump all threads; default false for bounded current-thread snapshot"},"max_threads":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000,"default":100,"description":"Cap on number of threads dumped"}},"required":["file"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"dumped":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if the dump call completed without raising"},"all_threads":{"type":"boolean"},"max_threads":{"type":"integer"},"handler_enabled":{"type":"boolean","description":"Value of faulthandler.is_enabled() observed after the dump"},"note":{"type":"string","description":"Static advisory text about ASCII-only, 500-char string limit, 100-frame/thread limit, reversed order"}},"required":["dumped","all_threads","max_threads","handler_enabled"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Writes a minimal traceback text to the supplied file/descriptor. Does not install signal handlers, does not start a watchdog thread, does not exit the process, does not allocate on the heap during the dump path. No persistent state change beyond bytes written to the target file.

Constraints Requires CPython with the C-implemented faulthandler module (added 3.3). max_threads keyword requires 3.15+. Passing a file descriptor requires 3.5+. The file must remain open and its descriptor stable for the duration of use; re-call after any replacement. Output is ASCII-only and minimal. register()/unregister() are unavailable on Windows; enable() installs a Windows exception handler on 3.6+. C stack dumping (dump_c_stack, c_stack) requires 3.14+ and OS backtrace(3)/dladdr1(3) support. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • file is closed or its descriptor was reused/dup2-replaced, so output goes to the wrong target
  • file is not writable or is a non-file object lacking fileno()/write support
  • max_threads out of range or non-integer
  • dump_traceback raises TypeError for invalid file argument
  • Output is truncated: ASCII-only with backslashreplace, 500-char string cap, 100 frames per thread, 100 threads default
  • No source lines shown; only filename, function name, line number
  • If the process is already in a fatal state, the dump may be incomplete or absent

Ranked use cases

  1. Bounded diagnostic snapshot of the current thread's Python stack written to a log file at a checkpoint, without enabling global fault handlers
  2. Pre-crash breadcrumb capture in long-running services by dumping the current thread to a rotating log before risky native calls
  3. Deadlock triage helper that dumps all threads (all_threads=true, capped max_threads) to a file on a watchdog timeout
  4. Test-harness assertion support that captures a minimal traceback to a buffer for later inspection when a check fails

fcntl

Unix-specific services

Python documentation

Advisory whole-file lock acquisition via fcntl.flock on a caller-supplied file descriptor, with non-blocking option and explicit release, returning a normalized lock state without exposing raw errno values.

APIs

  • fcntl.flock(fd, operation)
  • fcntl.LOCK_SH
  • fcntl.LOCK_EX
  • fcntl.LOCK_NB
  • fcntl.LOCK_UN

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"fd":{"type":"integer","description":"Integer file descriptor to lock"},"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["shared","exclusive","unlock"],"description":"Lock mode to apply"},"nonBlocking":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, OR LOCK_NB so the call fails instead of waiting"}},"required":["fd","mode"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"locked":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if the requested lock state is now held"},"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["shared","exclusive","unlock"]},"wouldBlock":{"type":"boolean","description":"True when nonBlocking was set and the lock was unavailable"}},"required":["locked","mode","wouldBlock"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects May block the calling thread until the lock is granted when nonBlocking is false; acquires or releases an advisory lock on the open file description associated with fd; no data is read or written and no file contents are modified. The lock is advisory and only coordinates with other flock-aware processes.

Constraints Unix only; not available on WASI. Requires a valid open file descriptor; on some systems LOCK_EX requires the descriptor to be opened for writing. flock semantics are per open file description and may be emulated via fcntl on some platforms, so behavior across NFS and other network filesystems is not guaranteed. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • OSError with EACCES or EAGAIN when nonBlocking is true and the lock is unavailable (mapped to wouldBlock=true, locked=false)
  • OSError with EBADF when fd is not a valid open file descriptor
  • OSError with EINVAL when the operation is unsupported by the underlying filesystem
  • OSError with EINTR surfaced if the underlying call is interrupted and not retried
  • TypeError when fd is not an integer or mode is not one of the enumerated values
  • ValueError when nonBlocking is combined with mode 'unlock'

Ranked use cases

  1. Serialize access to a shared state or cache file across cooperating worker processes before read-modify-write cycles.
  2. Implement a non-blocking single-instance guard so a second process can detect an already-running job and exit cleanly.
  3. Coordinate concurrent appends to a shared log or spool file using shared locks for readers and exclusive locks for writers.
  4. Provide a bounded, testable locking primitive for capability builders that need deterministic contention behavior without raw errno handling.
  5. Protect migration or export artifacts during batch processing so partial files are never consumed by downstream stages.

{"type":"object","properties":{"cacheHandle":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque handle to the memoized wrapper"},"parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"maxsize":{"type":["integer","null"]},"typed":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["maxsize","typed"]},"info":{"type":"object","properties":{"hits":{"type":"integer"},"misses":{"type":"integer"},"maxsize":{"type":["integer","null"]},"currsize":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["hits","misses","maxsize","currsize"]},"wrappedRef":{"type":"string","description":"Reference to original callable via __wrapped__"}},"required":["cacheHandle","parameters","info","wrappedRef"],"additionalProperties":false}

Not suitable for functions with side effects, generators, async functions, or impure functions (time(), random()). Keyword argument order affects cache key identity. Type specificity applies only to immediate arguments, not contents. Platform: CPython standard library; behavior may differ on non-CPython implementations.

  • TypeError at call time if arguments are unhashable (dict, list, set)

  2. Caching I/O-bound lookups such as static web content or PEP retrieval with a bounded maxsize to prevent unbounded growth
  3. Instrumenting cache effectiveness via cache_info() hits/misses to tune maxsize for a workload
  4. Providing a cache_clear() invalidation hook for configuration or data-refresh workflows

{"type":"object","properties":{"args":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Argument list to parse, excluding program name (typically sys.argv[1:])"},"shortopts":{"type":"string","description":"Short option letters; \u0027:\u0027 suffix means required argument, \u0027::\u0027 means optional argument; leading \u0027\u002B\u0027 or \u0027-\u0027 alters gnu_getopt scanning"},"longopts":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Long option names without leading \u0027--\u0027; \u0027=\u0027 suffix means required argument, \u0027=?\u0027 means optional argument"}},"required":["args","shortopts"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"options":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":["string","null"]},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2},"description":"Ordered (option, value) pairs; option prefixed with \u0027-\u0027 or \u0027--\u0027, value \u0027\u0027 when no argument, or null option with list value when \u0027-\u0027 scanning mode is active"},"remaining":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Positional arguments left after option processing"},"error":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"msg":{"type":"string"},"opt":{"type":"string"}},"required":["msg","opt"],"additionalProperties":false}},"required":["ok","options","remaining","error"],"additionalProperties":false}

Behavior differs from GNU getopt(): getopt() stops at first non-option, gnu_getopt() intermixes. Optional arguments require Python 3.14+. Long-option prefix matching is supported. Platform-independent pure Python, but POSIXLY_CORRECT environment influence is a portability consideration.

  • GetoptError raised when a required argument is missing for an option; surfaced as ok=false

{"type":"object","properties":{"pattern":{"type":"string","description":"Shell-style pathname pattern; may be absolute or relative"},"root_dir":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional root directory for relative patterns"},"recursive":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"include_hidden":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"max_results":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":100000,"description":"Hard cap on returned entries"},"sort":{"type":"boolean","default":true}},"required":["pattern","max_results"],"additionalProperties":false}

  • Name containing whitespace or leading '&' rejected as invalid input.

  • Unexpected module import failure surfaces as an internal error distinct from not-found.

Ranked use cases

  1. HTML/XML text unescaping pipelines that need exact named-reference resolution before decoding.
  2. Sanitizer or validator that verifies whether a named entity is valid HTML5 versus HTML4-only.
  3. Documentation and content migration tooling converting legacy HTML4 entities to Unicode.
  4. Test-fixture generation for parsers by enumerating entity-to-codepoint mappings.
  5. Data normalization for scraped markup where entity names must be canonicalized to Unicode characters.

Internet Protocols and Support

Python documentation

Perform a single bounded HTTP/HTTPS request: open an HTTPConnection or HTTPSConnection to a given host/port, send one request (method, path, optional body and headers), read the response status, reason, headers and a bounded body, then close the connection.

  • http.client.HTTPConnection

  • HTTPResponse.read
  • HTTPResponse.getheader
  • HTTPResponse.status
  • HTTPResponse.reason

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string","description":"Server hostname or host:port"},"port":{"type":["integer","null"],"minimum":1,"maximum":65535},"scheme":{"type":"string","enum":["http","https"]},"method":{"type":"string"},"path":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute request path per RFC 2616 5.1.2"},"headers":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},"body":{"type":["string","null"]},"timeout":{"type":["number","null"],"minimum":0},"maxBodyBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":65536}},"required":["host","scheme","method","path"],"additionalProperties":false}
