{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"integer"},"reason":{"type":"string"},"headers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}},"body":{"type":"string","description":"Body decoded as ISO-8859-1, truncated to maxBodyBytes"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"bytesRead":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["status","reason","headers","body","truncated","bytesRead"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Opens an outbound TCP (and for HTTPS, TLS) connection to the specified host and port, sends one HTTP request, reads a bounded portion of the response, and closes the connection. Emits auditing events http.client.connect and http.client.send. No local files are written; no state is retained between calls.

Constraints Not available on WASI/WebAssembly. HTTPS requires Python compiled with SSL support (ssl module). The path must be an absolute path per RFC 2616 5.1.2 unless using a proxy or OPTIONS/CONNECT. A Host header must be supplied or generated. Response body is capped by maxBodyBytes to keep the operation bounded. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • http.client.InvalidURL when port is non-numeric or empty
  • http.client.NotConnected when request is attempted without a connection
  • http.client.CannotSendRequest / CannotSendHeader / ResponseNotReady on improper connection state
  • http.client.BadStatusLine when the server returns an unparseable status line
  • http.client.RemoteDisconnected when the peer closes before any response data
  • http.client.IncompleteRead when the body ends prematurely
  • http.client.LineTooLong when a response line exceeds limits
  • socket.timeout / TimeoutError when timeout elapses
  • ssl.SSLError when TLS negotiation or certificate verification fails
  • OSError from the underlying socket
  • Body truncation flagged via truncated=true rather than an error

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders probing a known HTTP endpoint to verify reachability and capture status/headers for downstream tooling.
  2. Fetching a small, bounded JSON or text resource from a fixed host for ingestion into an agent workflow.
  3. Health-check style single-request diagnostics against an internal service, returning status and reason.
  4. Submitting a small form-encoded POST body to a fixed endpoint and capturing the response status and headers.
  5. Retrieving response headers only (e.g., via HEAD) to inspect content type, caching, or redirect metadata.

http.server

Internet Protocols and Support

Python documentation

Build a bounded, non-blocking static-file HTTP response plan: given a request path, a served root directory, and a set of extra response headers, compute the exact status line, header list, and body descriptor (file path or directory listing) that a SimpleHTTPRequestHandler subclass would emit for a GET/HEAD request, without opening a socket or serving traffic.

APIs

  • http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler (subclassed; provides do_GET/do_HEAD, guess_type, list_directory, index_pages, extensions_map, default_content_type, extra_response_headers)
  • http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler.send_response / send_header / end_headers (header emission semantics modeled by the plan)
  • http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler.date_time_string (RFC 7231 Date/Last-Modified formatting)
  • http.server.HTTPServer / ThreadingHTTPServer (server classes referenced only as the eventual host of the handler; not instantiated by this operation)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"rootDirectory":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute path of the directory to serve; must exist and be a directory."},"requestPath":{"type":"string","description":"URL path component including query, e.g. \u0027/sub/index.html?x=1\u0027."},"method":{"type":"string","enum":["GET","HEAD"]},"ifModifiedSince":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional If-Modified-Since header value in HTTP-date form."},"extraResponseHeaders":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2},"description":"Sequence of [name, value] pairs applied only to 200 responses."},"indexPages":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Filenames treated as directory index pages."},"defaultContentType":{"type":"string"},"followSymlinks":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["rootDirectory","requestPath","method","extraResponseHeaders","indexPages","defaultContentType","followSymlinks"]}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"statusCode":{"type":"integer"},"reasonPhrase":{"type":"string"},"headers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2}},"bodyKind":{"type":"string","enum":["file","directory-listing","empty","error-page"]},"bodyPath":{"type":["string","null"]},"contentLength":{"type":["integer","null"]},"contentType":{"type":["string","null"]},"lastModified":{"type":["string","null"]},"warnings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["statusCode","reasonPhrase","headers","bodyKind","bodyPath","contentLength","contentType","lastModified","warnings"]}

Effects Pure computation: reads directory metadata and file stat information under rootDirectory; performs no network I/O, binds no socket, starts no server, writes no files, and emits no logs to stderr. Returns a serializable plan only.

Constraints Design proposal only; not installed, not available on any worker, and not executed. http.server is documented as not recommended for production and as unavailable on WASI/WebAssembly. SimpleHTTPRequestHandler follows symbolic links, so callers must treat followSymlinks=false as advisory unless the host enforces it. send_header/send_response_only do not validate CRLF, so this operation must sanitize all header names/values itself. No TLS, no HTTP/1.1 persistent-connection semantics, and no authentication are modeled.

Failure modes

  • rootDirectory does not exist or is not a directory -> error result, no plan emitted
  • requestPath escapes rootDirectory via '..' or absolute path -> 404 plan plus warning
  • requestPath contains CR/LF or control characters -> rejected input error (header injection guard)
  • extraResponseHeaders contains CR/LF or attempts to override server-managed headers (Content-Type, Content-Length, Last-Modified, Server, Date) -> rejected or dropped with warning
  • ifModifiedSince is not a valid HTTP-date -> header ignored with warning
  • symlink target outside rootDirectory while followSymlinks is false -> 404 plan plus warning
  • unreadable file (permission denied) -> 404 'File not found' plan
  • directory listing fails (os.listdir error) -> 404 plan
  • method not in {GET, HEAD} -> rejected input error

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders can precompute and diff expected HTTP responses for static-asset fixtures without starting a server, enabling deterministic tests of handler subclasses.
  2. Security reviewers can enumerate which paths under a root would be served, including symlink escapes and directory listings, before exposing any server.
  3. Documentation and tutorial generators can produce accurate example response headers (Content-Type, Content-Length, Last-Modified) for SimpleHTTPRequestHandler lessons.
  4. CI linters can validate extra_response_headers and index_pages configurations for header-injection and override conflicts prior to deployment.
  5. Agent tooling can plan a bounded local file-serving step (status, headers, body descriptor) for review before any socketserver binding is attempted.

Graphical user interfaces with Tk

Python documentation

idlelib.syntax_check_source: perform a bounded, non-executing syntax check of a single Python source string using the same compile-based check that IDLE's 'Check Module' feature performs, returning a structured result (ok flag, error message, line/column offset) without launching IDLE, opening windows, or executing user code.

APIs

  • compile (builtin) — used to parse the source string in 'exec' mode and raise SyntaxError with lineno/offset/text attributes; this is the underlying mechanism IDLE's Check Module relies on
  • SyntaxError (builtin exception) — carries msg, lineno, offset, text and end_lineno/end_offset attributes that populate the structured error result
  • ast.parse — alternative parse-only path that yields the same SyntaxError information without producing a code object

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"source":{"type":"string","description":"Python source text to check"},"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Logical filename used in error messages; defaults to \u0027\u003Cstring\u003E\u0027"},"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["exec","eval","single"],"default":"exec"}},"required":["source"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"error":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"type":{"type":"string"},"message":{"type":"string"},"lineno":{"type":["integer","null"]},"offset":{"type":["integer","null"]},"end_lineno":{"type":["integer","null"]},"end_offset":{"type":["integer","null"]},"text":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["type","message","lineno","offset","end_lineno","end_offset","text"],"additionalProperties":false}},"required":["ok","error"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation: no files are written, no IDLE GUI or Tk window is created, no subprocess or RPC socket is opened, and no user code is executed. The operation only parses/compiles the provided string in memory. It does not read or modify ~/.idlerc configuration.

Constraints idlelib is documented as an optional module and its code (except Startup files) is 'private' per PEP 434, so this binding must not depend on private idlelib internals; it reimplements the documented Check Module behavior via public builtins. Requires a CPython build that includes idlelib only if any idlelib import is attempted; the proposed operation itself needs only compile/ast. No Tk display is required. Behavior of error offsets follows CPython's SyntaxError attributes and may vary across Python versions. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • SyntaxError raised by compile/ast.parse is caught and reported in the 'error' field rather than propagated
  • ValueError for null bytes in source is caught and reported as an error entry
  • TypeError if 'source' is not a string (schema violation) is rejected before the operation runs
  • MemoryError or RecursionError on pathologically large or deeply nested input is surfaced as an operation failure, not a syntax result
  • UnicodeDecodeError is not applicable since input is already a str; callers passing bytes must decode first

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight syntax validation of editor buffers before a user triggers Run Module, mirroring IDLE's Check Module without launching the GUI
  2. CI or lint gate that rejects files with syntax errors and reports line/column locations in a structured, machine-readable form
  3. Interactive teaching tool that explains syntax errors with precise positions, analogous to IDLE's error highlighting in the editor
  4. Batch validation of many source snippets (e.g., generated code) in a sandboxed, non-executing pass
  5. Editor/IDE integration that surfaces IDLE-equivalent syntax diagnostics via a stable JSON contract instead of private idlelib calls

APIs

  • imaplib.IMAP4
  • imaplib.IMAP4_SSL
  • IMAP4.login
  • IMAP4.select
  • IMAP4.uid
  • IMAP4.logout
  • IMAP4.error

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":65535},"use_ssl":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"timeout_seconds":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0},"username":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"password":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"mailbox":{"type":"string","default":"INBOX"},"search_charset":{"type":["string","null"],"default":null},"search_criteria":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"minItems":1}},"required":["host","username","password","search_criteria"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"response_code":{"type":"string"},"uids":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"uid_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"mailbox":{"type":"string"},"exists_count":{"type":["integer","null"]}},"required":["response_code","uids","uid_count","mailbox","exists_count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Opens an outbound TCP (optionally TLS) connection to the IMAP server, performs LOGIN (plaintext credentials over the wire unless TLS is used), issues SELECT with readonly=True, issues UID SEARCH, then LOGOUT. No messages are fetched, flagged, stored, copied, or expunged; mailbox contents are not modified. Auditing events imaplib.open and imaplib.send are raised. Credentials are transmitted to the remote server.

Constraints Not available on WASI/WebAssembly platforms. Requires network egress to the IMAP host and port (143 plain, 993 SSL by default). With IMAP4_SSL default ssl_context, the server certificate and hostname are NOT verified; callers needing verification must supply an ssl.SSLContext from ssl.create_default_context(). Message numbers are unstable across EXPUNGE, so UIDs are used exclusively. STATUS is not supported on IMAP4 (RFC 1730) servers. IMAP4_stream is out of scope for this operation. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • IMAP4.error raised on protocol or command errors (e.g., bad search criteria, authentication failure)
  • IMAP4.abort raised on server-side connection errors; instance must be discarded and recreated
  • IMAP4.readonly raised if a writable mailbox status changes unexpectedly (mitigated by read-only select)
  • socket.timeout or OSError on connection, TLS handshake, or read timeouts
  • ssl.SSLError on certificate/handshake failure when use_ssl is true
  • ValueError if timeout_seconds is zero (non-blocking socket rejected by open())
  • Invalid input rejected by schema validation before any network activity
  • Server returns NO/BAD for UID SEARCH; surfaced as IMAP4.error rather than silent empty result

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders: enumerate UIDs matching a criterion (e.g., UNSEEN, FROM) in a mailbox to drive downstream batch fetch pipelines without mutating state.

{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Absolute or relative module name, e.g. \u0027pkg.mod\u0027 or \u0027..mod\u0027."},"package":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Anchor package for relative names; required when name is relative."}},"required":["name"],"additionalProperties":false}

However, find_spec may import parent packages of a dotted name, which executes their code and mutates sys.modules; finders may perform filesystem or network I/O and populate sys.path_importer_cache.

  • ModuleNotFoundError when the parent package of a dotted name cannot be imported

  1. Pre-flight capability check: determine whether a named module can be located before attempting to import it, avoiding partial side effects.
  2. Dependency inventory: enumerate spec origins and package status for a set of module names to build a manifest of what a worker environment provides.
  3. Diagnostics for import failures: distinguish 'not found' from 'found but broken' by inspecting the resolved spec and loader class.
  4. Relative-import resolution: normalize relative names against a package anchor for tooling that rewrites or validates import statements.

Behavior of abstract-method sets depends on the Python version (e.g. load_module removed in 3.15, discover added in 3.15), so results are version-sensitive and must be reported with the interpreter version. Resolve a module's import specification without executing it: given a module name and optional package anchor, return a bounded summary of the located ModuleSpec (origin, whether it is a package, loader class name, and submodule search locations) using importlib.util.find_spec, without importing or executing the target module.

  • importlib.util.resolve_name(name, package) — converts a relative module name to an absolute one; used to normalize the requested name before lookup.
  • importlib.machinery.ModuleSpec — the spec object whose attributes (name, origin, submodule_search_locations, loader) are read to build the bounded output.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Module name, absolute or relative (leading dots allowed)."},"package":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Anchor package for relative names; required when name is relative."}},"required":["name"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"found":{"type":"boolean"},"resolvedName":{"type":"string"},"origin":{"type":["string","null"]},"isPackage":{"type":"boolean"},"loaderClass":{"type":["string","null"]},"submoduleSearchLocations":{"type":["array","null"],"items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["found","resolvedName","origin","isPackage","loaderClass","submoduleSearchLocations"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only with respect to the target module: no module code is executed and the target is not added to sys.modules by this operation. However, find_spec may import parent packages for dotted names, which can execute their code and mutate sys.modules; finders may perform filesystem I/O and populate sys.path_importer_cache. No files are written.

Constraints Pure-Python standard library; no installation or availability on any worker is claimed. Behavior depends on the interpreter's sys.path, sys.meta_path, sys.path_hooks and sys.implementation.cache_tag. Results are a point-in-time snapshot and may be stale after filesystem changes unless importlib.invalidate_caches() is called. Not thread-safe with concurrent imports/reloads.   • NotImplementedError or platform-specific errors from finders during meta_path search.
  • Returned found=false with null origin when no spec is located (not an error).

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight capability check: determine whether a module can be located before attempting to import it, enabling graceful degradation in plugin hosts.
  2. Dependency inventory and diagnostics: enumerate origins and package status of modules to build environment reports without executing third-party code.
  3. Custom importer/finder development: inspect what spec the standard machinery would produce for a name to validate a new MetaPathFinder or PathEntryFinder.
  4. Sandboxed or lazy loading orchestration: resolve specs and defer execution, feeding specs to module_from_spec only when needed.
  5. Relative-import resolution tooling: normalize and validate relative module names against a package anchor for static analysis or refactoring tools.

{"type":"object","properties":{"address":{"type":"string","description":"IP address literal, e.g. \u0027192.168.0.1\u0027 or \u00272001:db8::1\u0027"}},"required":["address"],"additionalProperties":false}

itertools

Functional Programming Modules

Python documentation

Bounded batch-and-accumulate over a finite JSON array: consume a finite list of numbers, group it into fixed-size tuples via itertools.batched, and compute running totals per batch via itertools.accumulate, returning a bounded, fully materialized result.

APIs

  • itertools.batched(iterable, n, *, strict=False) — groups input into tuples of length n, last batch may be shorter; raises ValueError if n < 1 or if strict and final batch is short
  • itertools.accumulate(iterable, function=operator.add, *, initial=None) — yields running accumulated totals; used here with default addition to produce per-batch running sums
  • itertools.islice(iterable, stop) — used internally by batched to bound consumption; documented as the truncation primitive for finite extraction

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"values":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"description":"Finite list of numeric values to process"},"batchSize":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Number of elements per batch (n for batched)"},"strict":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, reject a final batch shorter than batchSize"},"initial":{"type":["number","null"],"default":null,"description":"Optional initial value for accumulate; null means no initial"}},"required":["values","batchSize"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"batches":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"}},"description":"Input partitioned into tuples of length batchSize (last may be shorter unless strict)"},"runningTotals":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"}},"description":"Per-batch accumulate() output over each batch"},"batchCount":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"elementCount":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["batches","runningTotals","batchCount","elementCount"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation with no I/O, no filesystem, network, or process side effects. Inputs are fully consumed into memory (batched consumes lazily but the operation materializes all batches and totals into the returned JSON arrays). No global state is mutated.

Constraints Requires a Python runtime providing itertools.batched (added in 3.12; strict option added in 3.13) and itertools.accumulate (3.2+, initial in 3.8+). Input must be a finite JSON array; infinite iterators such as count(), cycle(), and repeat() without times are not representable and must not be used. Output size is O(len(values)); callers must cap input length. No installation, availability, or execution on any worker is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError if batchSize < 1 (batched requires n at least one)
  • ValueError if strict is true and the final batch is shorter than batchSize
  • TypeError if values contains non-numeric entries that cannot be added by the default accumulate function
  • TypeError if initial is provided and is not compatible with the numeric element type
  • Resource exhaustion if values is very large; caller must bound input size since output is fully materialized

Ranked use cases

  1. Streaming-style running totals over chunked numeric telemetry: batch a finite sample and compute per-batch cumulative sums for downstream aggregation.
  2. Chunked data validation and reshaping: partition a flat numeric array into fixed-size tuples (batched) with strict mode to enforce complete batches before further processing.
  3. Amortization/balance-style recurrence evaluation: apply accumulate with an initial value over a finite payment stream to produce a running balance table.
  4. Running maximum/minimum or running product summaries: reuse the same bounded batch-and-accumulate shape with min, max, or operator.mul as the accumulate function.
  5. Educational/recipe scaffolding for capability builders: demonstrate the documented iterator algebra (batched + accumulate + islice) as a composable, memory-bounded pattern for building larger pipelines.

{"type":"object","properties":{"valid":{"type":"boolean"},"normalized":{"type":["string","null"]},"topLevelType":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["object","array","string","number","boolean","null",null]},"byteLength":{"type":["integer","null"]},"error":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"msg":{"type":"string"},"pos":{"type":"integer"},"lineno":{"type":"integer"},"colno":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["msg","pos","lineno","colno"],"additionalProperties":false}},"required":["valid","normalized","topLevelType","byteLength","error"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"results":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"identifier":{"type":"string"},"isKeyword":{"type":"boolean"},"isSoftKeyword":{"type":"boolean"},"classification":{"type":"string","enum":["keyword","softkeyword","neither"]}},"required":["identifier","isKeyword","isSoftKeyword","classification"],"additionalProperties":false}},"keywordCount":{"type":"integer"},"softKeywordCount":{"type":"integer"},"kwlist":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"softkwlist":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["results","keywordCount","softKeywordCount"],"additionalProperties":false}

  • linecache.checkcache(filename=None) — validates cached entries against on-disk state so stale lines are not returned
  • linecache.clearcache() — clears the internal cache to bound memory and force re-reads
  • tokenize.open() — used internally by linecache to open files with detected encoding (defaults to UTF-8)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Path or module name to read from; may be relative, absolute, or a \u0027\u003Cfrozen ...\u003E\u0027 marker"},"lineno":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"1-based line number to retrieve"},"module_globals":{"type":["object","null"],"description":"Optional module globals dict used for __loader__/__file__ resolution; null if not applicable"},"refresh":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, call checkcache(filename) before reading to avoid stale cached lines"}},"required":["filename","lineno"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"line":{"type":"string","description":"The requested line including trailing newline if found, otherwise empty string"},"found":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if a non-empty line was returned"},"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Echo of the resolved filename argument"},"lineno":{"type":"integer","description":"Echo of the requested line number"}},"required":["line","found","filename","lineno"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints Process-local cache only; not shared across workers or processes. Requires filesystem read access to the target path or a resolvable loader in module_globals. Encoding detection depends on tokenize.detect_encoding with UTF-8 default. Frozen-module filename resolution requires module_globals with '__file__'. Behavior is CPython-version dependent (frozen-module support added in 3.14). No installation or availability on any worker is claimed.

  • Missing file: getline returns '' rather than raising; caller must interpret empty string as not-found
  • Out-of-range lineno: returns '' with no error signal
  • Encoding/decoding errors during tokenize.open: swallowed by getline, yielding ''
  • Loader get_source() returning None: yields ''
  • Stale cache entries if refresh is false and file changed on disk
  • Invalid lineno type (non-integer or <1): rejected by input schema validation before call

Ranked use cases

  1. Traceback enrichment: fetch source lines for frames to render formatted tracebacks (primary documented use)
  2. Diagnostic tooling: display the exact source line at a reported error location in logs or reports
  3. Code inspection utilities: random-access line lookup for linters, coverage reporters, or diff annotators
  4. Interactive debugging helpers: show surrounding source context for a given file and line number
  5. Frozen/loader-backed module introspection: resolve source lines for non-file-based modules via module_globals loaders

{"type":"object","properties":{"loggerName":{"type":"string","description":"Hierarchical logger name, typically __name__"},"level":{"type":"string","enum":["DEBUG","INFO","WARNING","ERROR","CRITICAL"]},"message":{"type":"string","description":"Format string or plain message"},"args":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Positional args merged into message via % formatting"},"extra":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true,"description":"Custom LogRecord attributes; keys must not clash with reserved LogRecord attributes"},"excInfo":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, attach current exception info (call only within an exception handler)"},"stackInfo":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"stackLevel":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"default":1}},"required":["loggerName","level","message"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"loggerName":{"type":"string"},"level":{"type":"string"},"levelno":{"type":"integer"},"effectiveLevel":{"type":"integer"},"enabled":{"type":"boolean","description":"Result of isEnabledFor for the requested level"},"emitted":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if the logging call was made (enabled and not disabled)"},"hasHandlers":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["loggerName","level","levelno","effectiveLevel","enabled","emitted","hasHandlers"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Reads logger hierarchy state (getLogger may create and register a new Logger in the manager's dict if absent). May write to configured handlers' destinations (files, streams, sockets) as a side effect of emission. Does not modify logger level, handlers, filters or propagate settings. Thread-safe per module guarantees via module-level and handler-level locks.

Behavior depends entirely on prior configuration (basicConfig, dictConfig, handlers); without handlers, records fall through to lastResort. excInfo must be used inside an exception handler. extra keys must avoid reserved LogRecord attribute names. No network, filesystem or subprocess access beyond what already-configured handlers perform. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • Invalid level string not in the enum or not resolvable via getLevelName -> ValueError/KeyError surfaced to caller
  • extra dict contains keys clashing with reserved LogRecord attributes (e.g. message, levelname, asctime) -> KeyError raised by logging internals
  • excInfo true but no active exception -> sys.exc_info() returns (None, None, None); record carries no traceback
  • Message formatting mismatch between message and args -> formatting error deferred to Formatter.format()/getMessage(), potentially swallowed by Handler.handleError when raiseExceptions is False
  • Handler emit failure (I/O error) -> routed to Handler.handleError; may be silently ignored depending on raiseExceptions
  • Logger disabled or level below effective threshold -> emitted false, no record produced (not an error)

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders emitting structured, level-gated diagnostic events from tool/agent code into the standard logging hierarchy for unified application logs
  2. Contextual audit/telemetry emission using extra to attach request IDs, user or client IP without changing call sites
  3. Safe conditional logging that first checks isEnabledFor to avoid expensive message construction when the level is filtered out
  4. Exception-aware error reporting from within except blocks using exc_info to capture tracebacks into configured handlers
  5. Library-facing logging facade that resolves module-level loggers via getLogger(__name__) so downstream applications retain fine-grained control

Compute the next rollover time and the set of backup files eligible for deletion for a TimedRotatingFileHandler configuration, without opening, creating, rotating or deleting any files.

APIs

  • logging.handlers.TimedRotatingFileHandler (constructor parameters when, interval, backupCount, utc, atTime, delay)
  • logging.handlers.TimedRotatingFileHandler.getFilesToDelete (returns absolute paths of oldest backup log files that would be deleted at rollover)
  • logging.handlers.TimedRotatingFileHandler.shouldRollover (determines whether enough time has passed for a rollover and computes the next rollover time)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Base log file path used to derive backup names; not opened."},"when":{"type":"string","enum":["S","M","H","D","W0","W1","W2","W3","W4","W5","W6","midnight"],"default":"h"},"interval":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"default":1},"backupCount":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":0},"utc":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"atTime":{"type":["string","null"],"pattern":"^([01][0-9]|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9](:[0-5][0-9])?$","description":"HH:MM or HH:MM:SS local/UTC time-of-day, or null."},"now":{"type":"string","format":"date-time","description":"Reference instant used for the computation."},"existingBackups":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Candidate backup file paths to evaluate for deletion."}},"required":["filename","when","interval","backupCount","now","existingBackups"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"nextRolloverAt":{"type":"string","format":"date-time"},"rolloverDue":{"type":"boolean"},"filesToDelete":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"effectiveIntervalSeconds":{"type":"integer"},"notes":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["nextRolloverAt","rolloverDue","filesToDelete","effectiveIntervalSeconds"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation only. No files are opened, created, renamed, rotated or deleted; no sockets, threads or handlers are instantiated. The proposal describes intended behavior and does not assert that any binding is installed, available on a worker, or executed.

Constraints Unix/Linux-oriented semantics for file naming and deletion ordering; Windows ST_INO behavior and exclusive file locks make WatchedFileHandler-style rotation inappropriate there. Deletion logic depends on the interval, so changing interval may leave stale backups. Rollover timing is computed at handler initialization and recomputed only on rollover, so results are advisory. Pickle-based network handlers are out of scope. No installation or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • Invalid 'when' value not in the documented set (S, M, H, D, W0-W6, midnight)
  • interval or backupCount negative or non-integer
  • atTime supplied but not parseable as a time-of-day, or supplied for intervals where it is ignored
  • now not a valid ISO-8601 date-time
  • existingBackups entries not sortable under the handler's date/time naming scheme, so deletion ordering is ambiguous
  • backupCount of 0 yields an empty filesToDelete list (no deletion)
  • Weekday-based rotation ignores interval, which may surprise callers

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight validation of a TimedRotatingFileHandler configuration before deploying a service, reporting the next rollover instant and which backups would be pruned.
  2. Capacity planning for log storage: estimate retention windows from backupCount and interval without touching the filesystem.
  3. Configuration review tooling that flags risky settings (backupCount=0, weekday rotation ignoring interval, atTime misuse) in logging configs.
  4. Migration auditing: compare existing backup files against the handler's deletion ordering to identify orphans left by interval changes.
  5. Test-fixture generation for logging configuration tests that need deterministic rollover timestamps and deletion sets without real I/O.

lzma

Data Compression and Archiving

Python documentation

Compress a bounded in-memory bytes payload into a single .xz container using lzma.compress with an explicit preset and integrity check, returning the compressed bytes and metadata.

APIs

  • lzma.compress(data, format=FORMAT_XZ, check=-1, preset=None, filters=None) — performs one-shot compression of a bytes object into a bytes object; the core API used by this operation.
  • lzma.is_check_supported(check) — used to validate that the requested integrity check (e.g. CHECK_CRC64, CHECK_SHA256) is available before compressing.
  • lzma.LZMAError — exception raised on compression/decompression or initialization errors, surfaced as a failure mode.
  • lzma.FORMAT_XZ, lzma.CHECK_CRC64, lzma.CHECK_CRC32, lzma.CHECK_NONE, lzma.PRESET_DEFAULT, lzma.PRESET_EXTREME — constants used to parameterize the operation.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bytes to compress (bounded size)."},"preset":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":9,"default":6},"extreme":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"check":{"type":"string","enum":["none","crc32","crc64","sha256"],"default":"crc64"}},"required":["data"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"compressed":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded .xz compressed bytes."},"inputBytes":{"type":"integer"},"outputBytes":{"type":"integer"},"format":{"type":"string","enum":["xz"]},"check":{"type":"string"},"preset":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["compressed","inputBytes","outputBytes","format","check","preset"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory computation; no filesystem, network or persistent state changes. Returns compressed bytes only.

Constraints Optional module — availability depends on the CPython build/distributor; not guaranteed. LZMAFile is not thread-safe, so concurrent use of a single instance requires external locking (this operation uses the stateless one-shot lzma.compress, avoiding that issue). Output format fixed to FORMAT_XZ; FORMAT_ALONE and FORMAT_RAW are out of scope. Input size and preset must be bounded to control memory. No installation, availability or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • LZMAError raised if the requested integrity check is not supported by the underlying liblzma build.
  • LZMAError raised during compression or compressor initialization.
  • Input rejected if data is not valid base64 or exceeds the bounded size limit.
  • Memory exhaustion at high presets (e.g. preset 9 can require up to ~800 MiB overhead) — operation must enforce a preset/size cap.
  • Module may be absent if CPython was built without the optional lzma module; callers must handle ImportError.

Ranked use cases

  1. Deterministic one-shot compression of bounded byte payloads for storage or transport, using lzma.compress with a fixed preset and CRC64 check.
  2. Integrity-checked archival of small artifacts where a verifiable .xz container with CRC32/CRC64/SHA256 is required.
  3. Pre-flight capability probe: combine is_check_supported with a tiny compress call to confirm the runtime supports a given check before bulk work.
  4. Reproducible test-fixture generation: produce .xz blobs at known presets for decompression round-trip tests.
  5. Size/ratio estimation for pipeline planning by compressing bounded samples at candidate presets before committing to a full job.

marshal

Data Persistence

Python documentation

marshal_roundtrip_bytes: serialize a bounded, allowlisted Python value to marshal bytes and immediately deserialize it back, returning the byte length, format version used, and a structural summary of the recovered value, with code objects disabled by default.

APIs

  • marshal.dumps(value, version, /, *, allow_code=True) — produces the bytes representation of a supported value; used for the encode step and to report the format version.
  • marshal.loads(bytes, /, *, allow_code=True) — decodes bytes back into a Python value; used for the decode step and to detect malformed input.
  • marshal.version — module-level constant indicating the default format version; used to validate the requested version.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"value":{"description":"A marshal-supported value: int, bool, float, complex, str, bytes, bytearray, tuple, list, dict, set, frozenset, slice, None, Ellipsis, StopIteration, or nested combinations thereof."},"version":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":6,"description":"Requested marshal format version; must not exceed marshal.version."},"allow_code":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"Whether code objects may be marshalled; defaults to false for safety."},"max_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1048576,"default":65536,"description":"Upper bound on serialized size; exceeding it aborts the operation."}},"required":["value"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"byte_length":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"version_used":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":6},"roundtrip_equal":{"type":"boolean"},"top_level_type":{"type":"string"},"error":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["ok","byte_length","version_used","roundtrip_equal","top_level_type","error"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory computation; no files are written and no persistent state is modified. Emits the marshal.dumps auditing event with arguments (value, version) and the marshal.loads auditing event with argument bytes. No network or filesystem access.

Constraints Format is Python-version-specific and undocumented; bytes produced under one interpreter version may not load under another, and code objects are explicitly not portable across versions. Not secure against malicious input; only operate on values produced within the same trusted process. Not a general persistence format; pickle/shelve are recommended for cross-version or untrusted data. Requires a CPython interpreter exposing the marshal module; behavior of version 5 (slice) and version 6 (frozendict) depends on the running interpreter version. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError when value or a nested element has an unsupported type (e.g. a custom class instance, function, or module).
  • ValueError when version exceeds marshal.version or is otherwise invalid.
  • ValueError when allow_code is false and the value contains a code object.
  • EOFError, ValueError, or TypeError from loads when the produced bytes are truncated or malformed (defensive check).
  • Size-limit failure when serialized output exceeds max_bytes.
  • TypeError when value is not a Python object representable in the marshal type set.
  • Note: dump() may write garbage before raising ValueError; this operation uses dumps() to avoid partial writes.

Ranked use cases

  1. Validating that a candidate value is marshal-serializable before writing a .pyc-style cache, catching unsupported types early.
  2. Producing a bounded, version-tagged byte blob for in-process caching of small configuration structures with a size cap.
  3. Round-trip conformance testing of marshal format versions 3–6 across supported container types (recursive lists, slices, frozendict).
  4. Sanity-checking that a code object is excluded when allow_code is false, enforcing a safe default for untrusted pipelines.
  5. Measuring serialized size of small data structures to inform cache sizing decisions without touching disk.

Python documentation

Compute a bounded, numerically robust scalar summary of a finite float sequence: accurate sum via math.fsum, product via math.prod, and Euclidean norm via math.hypot, returning all three plus finiteness flags.

APIs

  • math.fsum
  • math.prod
  • math.hypot
  • math.isfinite
  • math.isnan
  • math.isinf

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"values":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":0,"maxItems":100000},"start":{"type":"number","default":1}},"required":["values"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"sum":{"type":"number"},"product":{"type":"number"},"norm":{"type":"number"},"count":{"type":"integer"},"allFinite":{"type":"boolean"},"hasNaN":{"type":"boolean"},"hasInf":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["sum","product","norm","count","allFinite","hasNaN","hasInf"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation; no I/O, no mutation of caller data, no global state changes.

Constraints CPython math is a thin wrapper over the platform C math library; results may differ in the last ulp across platforms. math.fsum accuracy depends on IEEE-754 half-even rounding and may double-round on some non-Windows builds. Ranked use cases

  1. Accurate aggregate statistics (sum, product, L2 norm) for numeric feature vectors in data pipelines
  2. Numerically stable vector magnitude computation for geometry/physics coordinate arrays
  3. Detecting NaN/inf contamination in float datasets before downstream processing
  4. Computing product-of-elements and norm for probability or scaling factor arrays
  5. Building a reusable numeric summary primitive for capability builders composing math-based tools

math.integer

Numeric and Mathematical Modules

Python documentation

compute_integer_arithmetic: perform one bounded exact-integer computation (comb, factorial, gcd, isqrt, lcm, or perm) on caller-supplied integer arguments, returning the exact integer result.

APIs

  • math.integer.comb(n, k, /) — returns the exact binomial coefficient, zero when k > n, ValueError on negative arguments
  • math.integer.factorial(n, /) — returns the exact factorial of a nonnegative integer
  • math.integer.gcd(*integers) — returns the greatest common divisor of the arguments (0 for no arguments or all zeros)
  • math.integer.isqrt(n, /) — returns the floor of the exact integer square root of a nonnegative integer
  • math.integer.lcm(*integers) — returns the least common multiple of the arguments (1 for no arguments, 0 if any argument is zero)
  • math.integer.perm(n, k=None, /) — returns the exact number of ordered selections, defaulting k to n

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"function":{"type":"string","enum":["comb","factorial","gcd","isqrt","lcm","perm"]},"args":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":0,"maxItems":64,"description":"Positional integer arguments passed to the selected function; count must match the function\u0027s arity (comb: 2, factorial: 1, gcd: 0\u002B, isqrt: 1, lcm: 0\u002B, perm: 1 or 2)."}},"required":["function","args"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"function":{"type":"string","enum":["comb","factorial","gcd","isqrt","lcm","perm"]},"result":{"type":"integer","description":"Exact integer result of the computation."}},"required":["function","result"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation only: no filesystem, network, environment, or global state mutation. Returns a single exact integer; no side effects beyond CPU and memory consumption proportional to result size.

Constraints Requires Python 3.15+ where math.integer exists (module added in 3.15); not available on earlier interpreters. Arguments must be integers or objects implementing __index__; booleans are accepted as ints per Python semantics. Exact results can grow very large (factorial/comb/perm), so callers must bound input magnitude and result bit-length. Platform-independent pure-Python/C-level arithmetic; no OS-specific behavior. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError: negative argument supplied to comb, factorial, isqrt, or perm
  • ValueError: k > n is not an error for comb/perm (returns 0), but negative k or n is rejected
  • TypeError: argument does not implement __index__ (non-integer, float, or string)
  • ArityError: wrong number of positional arguments for the selected function (e.g., factorial with 2 args, comb with 1)
  • UnknownFunction: function name not in the allowed enum
  • ResourceLimit: result exceeds configured maximum integer bit-length or computation time budget
  • MemoryError: intermediate exact-integer computation exceeds available memory

Ranked use cases

  1. Combinatorial counting for test-case or configuration enumeration using comb and perm with exact results
  2. Cryptographic and number-theoretic helper computations using gcd and lcm for modular arithmetic scaffolding
  3. Exact factorial computation for probability, series, and benchmark workloads without floating-point error
  4. Integer square-root flooring for exact geometry, hashing, and fixed-point math via isqrt
  5. Bounded arithmetic primitive for capability builders needing deterministic, side-effect-free integer kernels in agent toolchains

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path of the file to map read-only."},"needle":{"type":"string","description":"Byte subsequence to search for, encoded as a string of bytes (latin-1 safe)."},"windowOffset":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Byte offset from file start of the mapping window; must be a multiple of ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY."},"windowLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Number of bytes to map starting at windowOffset."},"searchStart":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional start index within the mapped window for the search."},"searchEnd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional end index within the mapped window for the search."}},"required":["path","needle","windowOffset","windowLength"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"found":{"type":"boolean"},"firstIndex":{"type":["integer","null"],"description":"Lowest index within the mapped window where needle occurs, or null if not found."},"lastIndex":{"type":["integer","null"],"description":"Highest index within the mapped window where needle occurs, or null if not found."},"absoluteFirstOffset":{"type":["integer","null"],"description":"windowOffset \u002B firstIndex, or null."},"absoluteLastOffset":{"type":["integer","null"],"description":"windowOffset \u002B lastIndex, or null."},"windowOffset":{"type":"integer"},"windowLength":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["found","firstIndex","lastIndex","absoluteFirstOffset","absoluteLastOffset","windowOffset","windowLength"],"additionalProperties":false}

Unix and Windows constructor signatures differ; this design uses the portable access=ACCESS_READ keyword and avoids tagname, flags, and prot. windowOffset must be a multiple of ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY (equal to PAGESIZE on Unix). On Windows an empty file cannot be mapped. resize(), flush(), madvise(), and set_name() are out of scope.   • PermissionError when the file cannot be opened read-only
  • ValueError when windowOffset is not a multiple of ALLOCATIONGRANULARITY

  • ValueError on use of a closed map if close ordering is mishandled

  1. Fast substring/record scanning in large log or data files without loading them fully into memory
  2. Locating delimiter or magic-byte boundaries in binary artifacts for parsers and validators
  3. Building a bounded index of occurrences (first/last) for downstream chunked processing
  4. Read-only integrity checks that confirm expected markers exist within a specific file region
  5. Efficient search over memory-mapped fixtures in test harnesses without full reads

msvcrt

MS Windows Specific Services

Python documentation

Lock a byte range of an open file descriptor using msvcrt.locking with a caller-specified LK_* mode, returning the resulting lock state and the descriptor's current position.

APIs

  • msvcrt.locking(fd, mode, nbytes)
  • msvcrt.LK_LOCK
  • msvcrt.LK_NBLCK
  • msvcrt.LK_UNLCK

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"fd":{"type":"integer","description":"C runtime file descriptor from which the lock region starts at the current file position"},"mode":{"type":"string","enum":["LK_LOCK","LK_RLCK","LK_NBLCK","LK_NBRLCK","LK_UNLCK"],"description":"Lock mode constant name to pass to msvcrt.locking"},"nbytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Number of bytes in the region, may extend beyond end of file"}},"required":["fd","mode","nbytes"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"locked":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if the operation completed without OSError"},"fd":{"type":"integer"},"mode":{"type":"string"},"nbytes":{"type":"integer"},"position":{"type":"integer","description":"File position at time of call, the start of the locked region"}},"required":["locked","fd","mode","nbytes","position"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects May block the calling thread for up to roughly 10 seconds when using LK_LOCK or LK_RLCK on a contended region. Mutates OS-level file lock state for the descriptor; no data is written to the file. Emits the msvcrt.locking auditing event.

Constraints Windows only (module availability is Windows). Requires a valid C runtime file descriptor, typically obtained via os.open or msvcrt.open_osfhandle. Lock regions are per-descriptor and must not overlap; each region must be unlocked individually. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • OSError raised by msvcrt.locking when the region cannot be locked (immediately for LK_NBLCK/LK_NBRLCK, after 10 one-second retries for LK_LOCK/LK_RLCK)
  • OSError when fd is not a recognized file descriptor
  • OSError when unlocking a region that was not previously locked with LK_UNLCK
  • Overlapping lock regions are rejected; adjacent regions are not merged and must be unlocked individually
  • Auditing event msvcrt.locking is raised with arguments fd, mode, nbytes
  • Invalid mode name rejected before any call is made

Ranked use cases

  1. Serialize access to a shared file region across multiple Windows processes using LK_NBLCK with immediate failure for non-blocking coordination.
  2. Implement a bounded retry lock acquisition using LK_LOCK for cooperative writers that can tolerate up to ~10 seconds of waiting.
  3. Release a previously acquired region deterministically with LK_UNLCK in cleanup paths to avoid leaked locks.
  4. Guard a fixed-size record in a flat-file database by locking exactly nbytes at the record offset.
  5. Build a capability that probes lockability of a region non-destructively before committing to a write, using LK_NBLCK followed by LK_UNLCK.

probe_multiprocessing_start_methods: read-only capability probe that reports the supported start methods, the current global start method (without forcing it), and platform availability, using get_all_start_methods() and get_start_method(allow_none=True) so callers can plan a bounded worker-pool design without mutating global state.

APIs

  • multiprocessing.get_all_start_methods()
  • multiprocessing.get_start_method(allow_none=True)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"include_default":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, also report the first entry of get_all_start_methods() as the platform default."}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"supported":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","enum":["fork","spawn","forkserver"]},"description":"Start methods reported as supported on this platform."},"current":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["fork","spawn","forkserver",null],"description":"Current global start method, or null if not yet set (allow_none=True)."},"default":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["fork","spawn","forkserver",null],"description":"Platform default (first supported entry) when include_default is true, else null."}},"required":["supported","current","default"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only with respect to process creation: no child processes are spawned, no queues/pipes/locks are created, and the global start method is not forced (allow_none=True avoids setting it). No filesystem or network effects.

Constraints Availability: not Android, not iOS, not WASI; not supported on mobile or WebAssembly platforms. Runs on POSIX and Windows. 'fork' is POSIX-only; 'forkserver' requires POSIX with file-descriptor passing over Unix pipes (e.g., Linux) and a writable temporary directory. As of 3.14 'fork' is no longer the default on any platform; 'forkserver' is default on POSIX where available, otherwise 'spawn'. The global start method can only be set once; this probe deliberately avoids setting it. Child-process functionality requires an importable __main__ module. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • NotImplementedError if the platform cannot enumerate start methods (unexpected; surfaced as error).
  • ValueError from get_start_method if an invalid allow_none combination is used (not expected with allow_none=True).
  • ImportError when shared semaphore support is missing on the host, which can affect related multiprocessing primitives even though this probe itself does not instantiate queues.
  • Probe must not be relied upon to reflect later state; another component may call set_start_method() after the probe returns.

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders can pre-flight which start methods a host supports before designing a bounded Pool/Process fan-out, avoiding runtime ValueError from get_context().
  2. Detect whether the global start method is already set (current != null) so a library can honor a user-supplied context instead of forcing its own, per the documentation's library guidance.
  3. Choose between 'spawn' and 'forkserver' for portability planning on POSIX hosts, accounting for the writable-tempdir requirement of forkserver.
  4. Guard against unsafe 'fork' usage in multithreaded hosts by confirming whether fork is even offered and whether the default avoids it.
  5. Feed platform capability metadata into a scheduling/planning layer that decides whether process-based parallelism is viable versus thread-based alternatives.

Python documentation

multiprocessing.dummy.Pool.map: bounded thread-pool map over a list of inputs using the thread-backed dummy Pool, returning results in input order.

APIs

  • multiprocessing.dummy.Pool
  • multiprocessing.dummy.Pool.map
  • multiprocessing.dummy.Pool.close
  • multiprocessing.dummy.Pool.join

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Input values passed to the callable, in order."},"callableRef":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path of a module-level callable, e.g. \u0027math.sqrt\u0027."},"processes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Number of worker threads in the dummy Pool."},"chunksize":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Optional chunk size hint for map."}},"required":["items","callableRef","processes"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"results":{"type":"array","items":{},"description":"Results in the same order as input items."},"count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of results returned."}},"required":["results","count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Spawns up to processes worker threads in the calling process; runs the callable concurrently on each item; blocks until all items complete or an exception propagates; closes and joins the pool before returning. No subprocesses are created and no files or network resources are touched by the binding itself.

Constraints multiprocessing.dummy is thread-based, so it is bounded by the GIL and offers no CPU parallelism; it is useful only for I/O-bound or blocking work. The callable must be importable by dotted path (module-level). The dummy Pool API mirrors multiprocessing.Pool but uses threads. Platform availability follows the multiprocessing package (not Android, not iOS, not WASI). This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • callableRef cannot be imported or is not callable (ImportError/TypeError)
  • callable raises an exception; map propagates the first exception and aborts remaining work
  • items is not a list/iterable or is empty (empty returns empty results)
  • processes < 1 rejected by validation
  • chunksize < 1 rejected by validation
  • Pool creation fails if thread resources are unavailable (RuntimeError)
  • results not picklable is not an issue for threads, but non-serializable return values may still fail downstream consumers

Ranked use cases

  1. Parallelize blocking I/O calls (HTTP fetches, file reads) across a bounded thread pool without process overhead.
  2. Provide a drop-in thread-backed Pool for code written against the multiprocessing.Pool API that must run in environments where subprocess spawning is restricted.
  3. Batch-transform a list of records with a pure module-level function while preserving input order.
  4. Cap concurrency for rate-limited external services by fixing the number of worker threads.
  5. Serve as a portable fallback when process-based parallelism is unavailable or undesirable, keeping the same map/close/join lifecycle.

{"type":"object","properties":{"func_ref":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path \u0027module:qualname\u0027 of a module-level picklable callable"},"items":{"type":"array","description":"Picklable input values, bounded length","items":{}},"processes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":64},"start_method":{"type":"string","enum":["spawn","fork","forkserver"]},"timeout_seconds":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0}},"required":["func_ref","items","processes","start_method","timeout_seconds"],"additionalProperties":false}

multiprocessing.shared_memory

Concurrent Execution

Python documentation

create_shared_memory_block: allocate a new named POSIX-style shared memory block of a requested byte size via SharedMemory(create=True, size=N, track=...) and return its name, actual size and buffer length, without attaching, writing, closing or unlinking it.

APIs

  • multiprocessing.shared_memory.SharedMemory(name=None, create=True, size=N, *, track=True) — allocates a new shared memory block and exposes .name, .size and .buf
  • SharedMemory.name — read-only unique block name returned so other processes can attach
  • SharedMemory.size — read-only actual allocated size in bytes (may exceed requested size due to page granularity)
  • SharedMemory.buf — memoryview over the block, used only to report len(buf)
  • SharedMemory.close() — documented lifecycle method; referenced for caller-side cleanup guidance, not invoked by this operation
  • SharedMemory.unlink() — documented lifecycle method; referenced for caller-side cleanup guidance, not invoked by this operation

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"size":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Requested number of bytes for the new shared memory block"},"name":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional explicit unique block name; null lets the implementation generate one"},"track":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Register with a resource tracker where the OS does not do so automatically; ignored on Windows"}},"required":["size"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string","description":"Unique name of the created shared memory block"},"requestedSize":{"type":"integer","description":"Size in bytes as requested by the caller"},"actualSize":{"type":"integer","description":"Actual allocated size in bytes as reported by SharedMemory.size"},"bufferLength":{"type":"integer","description":"Length of the memoryview from SharedMemory.buf"},"tracked":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether resource tracking was requested for this block"}},"required":["name","requestedSize","actualSize","bufferLength","tracked"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Allocates a new OS-level shared memory segment that may outlive the creating process; the caller is responsible for calling close() on its handle and unlink() exactly once when the block is no longer needed by any process. No data is written, no existing block is attached, and no unlink is performed by this operation.

Constraints POSIX-style shared memory only (not distributed shared memory); availability and naming rules are platform-dependent; actual size may exceed the requested size due to memory page granularity; track is ignored on Windows, which deletes blocks when all handles close; processes not created via multiprocessing facilities may each get their own resource tracker, so track=False is advised when another process performs bookkeeping; this is a design proposal and does not assert installation, availability on any worker, or execution.

Failure modes

  • ValueError when size is not a positive integer or exceeds platform limits
  • FileExistsError when create=True and the supplied name already identifies an existing block
  • OSError/ENOSPC or platform-specific allocation failure when the OS cannot reserve the requested memory
  • PermissionError when the process lacks rights to create shared memory segments
  • Name collision or invalid name characters rejected by the underlying platform
  • Resource tracker unavailable or failing to register the block when track=True

Ranked use cases

  1. Zero-copy handoff of large numeric arrays between worker processes (e.g., NumPy buffers) to avoid serialization and socket/disk copying
  2. Shared result aggregation across forked worker processes, such as partial sums written into a common block
  3. Low-latency inter-process data plane for pipelines that would otherwise pay pickle/socket overhead
  4. Backing store for fixed-size shared structures (e.g., ShareableList-style records) managed by a SharedMemoryManager lifecycle
  5. Benchmarking and profiling shared-memory throughput versus message-passing transports in capability-building experiments

Read a bounded byte range from an open file descriptor without changing the file offset, using os.pread, returning the bytes read and an end-of-file indicator.

  • os.open(path, flags, mode=0o777, *, dir_fd=None) — low-level open returning a non-inheritable file descriptor; used by callers to obtain the fd consumed by the operation.
  • os.close(fd) — closes a file descriptor; used by callers to release the fd after the bounded read.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"fd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Open file descriptor to read from."},"length":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":1048576,"description":"Maximum number of bytes to read (bounded)."},"offset":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Absolute byte offset at which to read."}},"required":["fd","length","offset"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Bytes read, base64-encoded."},"bytesRead":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of bytes actually read."},"eof":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if fewer than length bytes were returned, indicating end of file."}},"required":["data","bytesRead","eof"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints os.pread is documented as Unix-only; not available on Windows or WASI. Requires a valid, seekable file descriptor opened by the caller. Read length is capped to bound memory use.   • OSError (EINVAL) if offset is negative or the descriptor does not support seeking.
  • OSError (EISDIR) if fd refers to a directory.
  • OSError (ESPIPE) if fd refers to a pipe or other non-seekable object.
  • TypeError if fd, length, or offset are not integers.
  • ValueError if length exceeds the configured bound.
  • InterruptedError is retried per PEP 475 rather than surfaced.

Ranked use cases

  1. Bounded random-access reads of large log or data files without disturbing a shared file offset.
  2. Concurrent multi-threaded readers over a single descriptor, each reading disjoint ranges safely.
  3. Chunked streaming of large files for hashing or transfer with explicit offset control.
  4. Peek/inspect a header or record at a known offset before deciding on further processing.
  5. Resumable reads after interruption by re-issuing at a recorded offset rather than seeking.

Python documentation

Enumerate submodules of a package path using pkgutil.iter_modules, returning a bounded, sorted list of ModuleInfo records (name, ispkg) without importing the submodules.

APIs

  • pkgutil.iter_modules(path=None, prefix='') — yields pkgutil.ModuleInfo namedtuples (module_finder, name, ispkg) for submodules found on the given path list; used as the core enumeration primitive.
  • pkgutil.ModuleInfo(module_finder, name, ispkg) — namedtuple describing a discovered module; its name and ispkg fields are projected into the output records.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"List of filesystem paths to scan; if omitted, top-level modules on sys.path are scanned."},"prefix":{"type":"string","default":"","description":"String prepended to every emitted module name."},"limit":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":10000,"default":1000,"description":"Maximum number of ModuleInfo records to return."}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"port":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":65535},"use_ssl":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"timeout":{"type":"number","exclusiveMinimum":0},"username":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"password":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"max_messages":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":10000,"default":1000}},"required":["host","username","password"],"additionalProperties":false}

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ncalls":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1000000,"description":"Number of Python calls per calibration run passed to Profile.calibrate."},"repeats":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":25,"default":5,"description":"Number of calibration runs whose results are aggregated."},"timerName":{"type":"string","enum":["perf_counter","process_time"],"default":"perf_counter","description":"Named stdlib timer used as the Profile timer callable."},"timeunit":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"default":0.0,"description":"Multiplier for integer timer units."}},"required":["ncalls"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"bias":{"type":"number","description":"Median computed per-event overhead in seconds."},"samples":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"description":"Per-run calibration values returned by Profile.calibrate."},"ncalls":{"type":"integer"},"repeats":{"type":"integer"},"timerName":{"type":"string"},"consistent":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if sample spread is within a small relative tolerance."}},"required":["bias","samples","ncalls","repeats","timerName","consistent"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only with respect to user code: no profiling is enabled on live code, no stats files are written, and no global profile.Profile.bias is mutated. Only CPU time is consumed for the bounded calibration runs; the returned bias is reported to the caller and not applied anywhere.

Constraints Deprecated since Python 3.15 and scheduled for removal in 3.17; this is a design proposal only and is not claimed to be installed, available on any worker, or executed. Calibration accuracy is bounded by the underlying clock resolution (typically ~1 ms) and may yield negative per-event values at low call counts. Pure-Python implementation has significant overhead. Timer callables must return a single number or a list of numbers; os.times()-style tuples are accepted by profile but discouraged. Platform clock behavior differs across OSes.

  • ncalls or repeats outside allowed bounds -> validation error before any calibration run
  • timerName not in the allowed enum -> validation error

  • module unavailable in the target interpreter -> import error surfaced, not masked

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders generating calibrated bias constants for deterministic profiling on a given platform before collecting stats.
  2. Tooling that compares profile vs profiling.tracing overhead to justify migration decisions.
  3. Test harnesses validating that a custom timer callable yields consistent calibration results.
  4. Documentation and tutorial generators producing platform-specific calibration examples.
  5. Regression checks that detect clock-resolution or timer regressions across Python builds.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"profilePath":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path to a binary profile file previously captured by the sampling profiler."},"format":{"type":"string","enum":["pstats","collapsed","flamegraph","gecko","heatmap"],"description":"Desired output format."},"outputPath":{"type":"string","description":"Destination file or directory; if omitted, format default applies (stdout for pstats, generated filename otherwise)."},"opcodes":{"type":"boolean","description":"Include bytecode opcode annotations where the format supports it.","default":false}},"required":["profilePath","format"],"additionalProperties":false}

pty

Unix-specific services

Python documentation

open_pty_pair: open a new pseudo-terminal master/slave file descriptor pair via pty.openpty() and return the descriptors with metadata, without spawning or attaching any process.

APIs

  • pty.openpty() — opens a new pseudo-terminal pair and returns (master, slave) file descriptors; this is the core API the operation wraps.
  • os.openpty() — underlying implementation pty.openpty() delegates to when available; role is the platform primitive for allocating the pty pair.
  • os.close() — used to release descriptors on failure paths so the operation does not leak fds.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"close_on_failure":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If true, close any partially opened descriptors before raising."}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"master_fd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"slave_fd":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"platform":{"type":"string"},"inheritable":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["master_fd","slave_fd","platform","inheritable"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Allocates two OS file descriptors (master and slave) in the calling process; no child process is created, no data is read or written, and no terminal state is modified beyond pty allocation. Descriptors remain open until the caller closes them.

Constraints Unix-only (Linux, FreeBSD, macOS primarily tested; other POSIX platforms untested). Not available on Windows. Descriptors are non-inheritable by default in Python 3.15+. Must not be mixed with higher-level system APIs on macOS per pty.fork() warning context. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • OSError/ENOSYS when the platform lacks pseudo-terminal support (non-Unix).
  • OSError/EMFILE or ENFILE when the process or system file descriptor limit is exhausted.
  • OSError/EACCES or EPERM when the process lacks permission to allocate a pty.
  • Descriptor leak if close_on_failure is false and a later step fails; caller must close fds.
  • Returned descriptors are process-local and invalid after fork/exec unless explicitly handled.

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders needing a raw pty pair to drive interactive CLI programs programmatically (read/write master, feed slave as child stdio).
  2. Terminal session recording/replay tooling analogous to script(1) that requires a controllable pseudo-terminal.
  3. Test harnesses that emulate a controlling terminal for programs that insist on TTY detection.
  4. Interactive automation of REPLs or password-prompting tools that refuse piped stdin.
  5. Sandboxed command execution wrappers that need isolated terminal semantics per job.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"module":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted module name to read, e.g. \u0027pkg.sub\u0027."},"path":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional sequence of directory paths prepended to sys.path for locating source."},"max_depth":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Maximum nesting depth of children to include; 0 means top-level only."},"include_bases":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to include class base names in output."}},"required":["module"],"additionalProperties":false}

Behavior depends on sys.path and the supplied path. Descriptors are pyclbr objects and must be serialized to plain JSON-compatible structures. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError-like lookup failure when the named module's source cannot be located on the given path or sys.path.
  • SyntaxError or other parse errors when the target source is not valid Python.

Concurrent Execution

Python documentation

bounded_put_with_timeout: attempt a single non-blocking-or-timeout-bounded insertion of one item into a caller-supplied queue.Queue instance, returning whether the item was accepted and the queue's approximate size afterward, without ever blocking indefinitely.

APIs

  • queue.Queue.put(item, block=True, timeout=None)
  • queue.Queue.qsize()
  • queue.Full
  • queue.ShutDown

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"item":{"description":"Opaque item to enqueue; must be JSON-serializable for transport but is passed through unchanged to the queue."},"block":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"timeout":{"type":["number","null"],"minimum":0,"default":null,"description":"Seconds to wait at most; null means no timeout (caller must accept potential blocking)."}},"required":["item"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"accepted":{"type":"boolean"},"qsize":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"reason":{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["full","shutdown",null]}},"required":["accepted","qsize","reason"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Mutates the caller-supplied queue by inserting at most one item; increments the unfinished-task counter used by join()/task_done(). No filesystem, network or process-level side effects. No installation or execution is performed or claimed.

Constraints Requires a live queue.Queue (or subclass) instance supplied by the caller; not usable across processes (multiprocessing.Queue is out of scope). Queue classes are not reentrant within a thread. On Windows and pre-3.0 POSIX, block=True with timeout=None performs an uninterruptible wait, so callers should prefer an explicit timeout. ShutDown semantics require Python 3.13+. SimpleQueue lacks task tracking and is excluded from this operation.

Failure modes

  • queue.Full raised when block is false or timeout elapses with no free slot; mapped to accepted=false, reason="full".
  • queue.ShutDown raised when the target queue has been shut down; mapped to accepted=false, reason="shutdown".
  • TypeError/ValueError from invalid timeout (negative or non-numeric) rejected before calling put().
  • Non-serializable item rejected at the transport boundary before reaching the queue.
  • qsize() is approximate; reported size may not reflect concurrent producers/consumers.

Ranked use cases

  1. Bounded producer hand-off: enqueue work items into a fixed-size FIFO with a timeout so a producer thread degrades gracefully instead of blocking forever when consumers stall.
  2. Backpressure signaling in a pipeline: detect queue.Full to throttle or shed load and report qsize for observability.
  3. Graceful shutdown coordination: detect queue.ShutDown to stop producers cleanly after shutdown(immediate=False) drains remaining tasks.
  4. Priority scheduling: apply the same bounded-put contract to a PriorityQueue carrying (priority, data) tuples for ordered task dispatch.
  5. Test harness for concurrency code: deterministically exercise Full/ShutDown paths by controlling maxsize and shutdown state.

Python documentation
