APIs

  • random.Random(seed) — constructs an independent generator instance so state is not shared with the global generator
  • random.Random.sample(population, k) — performs sampling without replacement and returns a new list in selection order
  • random.Random.getstate() — captures the generator's internal state so a later call can resume the same reproducible sequence

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"seed":{"type":["integer","string","null"],"description":"Seed for the isolated Random instance; null means system-derived seeding"},"population":{"type":"array","items":{},"minItems":1,"description":"Sequence of candidate items; may contain duplicates"},"k":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of unique positions to sample without replacement"}},"required":["seed","population","k"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure computation in memory; no filesystem, network or global generator mutation. The global random module state is untouched because a dedicated Random instance is used. Output is deterministic for a given seed and Python version.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"mod_name":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute module name, e.g. \u0027pkg.mod\u0027 or \u0027pkg\u0027."},"run_name":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional __name__ override; null means default."},"init_globals":{"type":["object","null"],"description":"Optional JSON object of pre-populated globals; must be JSON-serializable and is not modified."},"include_globals":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional allowlist of global names to report; empty means report only the special names."}},"required":["mod_name"],"additionalProperties":false}

Not thread-safe for sys manipulation; callers in threaded code should serialize or delegate to a separate process. __cached__ is no longer set as of 3.15; __loader__/__package__ setting deprecated since 3.12. Functions/classes defined by executed code are not guaranteed to work after return; importlib is preferred when that matters. This is a design proposal only — no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

  • ValueError or TypeError for a non-absolute or malformed mod_name.
  • Any exception raised by the executed module code propagates; the binding reports it as a structured error and does not swallow it.
  • Non-JSON-serializable init_globals rejected before execution.
  • Package without a __main__ submodule fails when executed as a package.
  • Partial side effects (cached imports, module-level state) persist in the process even on failure, since runpy is not a sandbox.

  1. Capability builders implementing a safe '-m'-style module launcher that reports resolved spec, file and globals summary.

  5. Diagnostics for package __main__ resolution (spec name, file, package) across sys.path entries.

Data Persistence

Python documentation

Open a shelf, read a single string key, and close it within one bounded call (read-only, no writeback), returning the deserialized value or a not-found indicator.

APIs

  • shelve.open(filename, flag='r', protocol=None, writeback=False, *, serializer=None, deserializer=None)
  • Shelf.close()
  • Shelf.__getitem__ (d[key])
  • Shelf.__contains__ (key in d)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Base filename of the shelf; underlying dbm may append an extension."},"key":{"type":"string","description":"Ordinary string key to look up."},"flag":{"type":"string","enum":["r"],"default":"r","description":"Read-only open flag; write flags are rejected by this operation."}},"required":["filename","key"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"found":{"type":"boolean"},"value":{"description":"Deserialized value when found; null when not found."},"key":{"type":"string"}},"required":["found","key"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only: opens the shelf with flag 'r', reads one key, and closes it explicitly. No writes, no sync of modified entries, no reorganize. May create no files; underlying dbm may still touch lock or metadata files depending on implementation.

  • UnpicklingError or arbitrary exception from deserializer when stored bytes are corrupt or incompatible
  • ShelveError if serializer/deserializer are supplied inconsistently (not used by this read-only operation)
  • Security: loading a shelf from an untrusted source can execute arbitrary code via pickle

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders reading a single persisted configuration or state value from a shelf without exposing full shelf mutation semantics.
  2. Safe inspection of legacy shelve-based caches during migration to a modern store, one key at a time.
  3. Test fixtures that verify a value was persisted to a shelf by a prior step, read-only.

shlex

Unix-specific services

Python documentation

tokenize_shell_like_string: lexically split a single input string into shell-like tokens using shlex.split with explicit comments and posix mode flags, returning the ordered token list and a count.

APIs

  • shlex.split(s, comments=False, posix=True) — performs the shell-like lexical split and returns the token list; core API for this operation.
  • shlex.shlex(instream, posix, punctuation_chars) — underlying lexer class whose POSIX/non-POSIX parsing rules govern split() behavior; referenced for mode semantics.
  • shlex.quote(s) — shell-escapes a string as a single safe token; referenced as the inverse-safety counterpart for downstream use of tokens.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"text":{"type":"string","description":"The string to tokenize."},"comments":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, enable comment parsing (commenters default \u0027#\u0027); if false, disable comment parsing."},"posix":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If true, use POSIX parsing rules; if false, use non-POSIX compatibility mode."}},"required":["text"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"tokens":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Ordered list of tokens produced by the split."},"count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Number of tokens returned."},"posix":{"type":"boolean","description":"Echo of the parsing mode used."},"comments":{"type":"boolean","description":"Echo of the comment-parsing flag used."}},"required":["tokens","count","posix","comments"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory computation; no filesystem, network, subprocess or environment mutation. No shell is invoked and no command is executed. The operation only reads the provided string and returns derived data.

Constraints Unix-shell-oriented semantics only; quote()/join() are not guaranteed correct for non-POSIX or Windows shells. punctuation_chars is not exposed by this bounded operation (split() does not accept it). posix defaults to true in split() but false in the shlex class constructor. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError raised by shlex.split on malformed input such as an unterminated quote.
  • TypeError if text is not a string (e.g. None); note the docs state passing None for s now raises an exception rather than reading sys.stdin.
  • Unexpected token boundaries when posix=false is requested, since non-POSIX rules differ (quotes not stripped, escapes not recognized, empty quoted strings not parseable).
  • Comment characters inside quoted regions may be treated differently than callers expect when comments=true; results depend on lexer state.
  • No semantic validation of tokens: punctuation or shell operators may be returned as tokens that are not valid shell syntax.

Ranked use cases

  1. Safely tokenizing user-supplied command-line strings into argument lists for downstream validation before any execution decision.
  2. Parsing run-control or minilanguage configuration lines that resemble shell syntax.
  3. Pre-flight inspection of remote command strings (e.g. ssh payloads) by splitting them into tokens for auditing.
  4. Building a capability that normalizes and compares shell-like argument strings without invoking a shell.
  5. Round-trip tooling: split a command string, then re-escape tokens with shlex.quote/join to produce injection-safe representations.

signal

Networking and Interprocess Communication

Python documentation

describe_signal: given a signal number, return a bounded, read-only description of that signal using signal.strsignal() and signal.Signals, without installing handlers, sending signals, or altering masks.

APIs

  • signal.strsignal(signalnum) — returns the human-readable description of a signal number (e.g. 'Interrupt' for SIGINT) or None if no description exists; raises ValueError for invalid numbers.
  • signal.Signals — IntEnum collection of SIG* constants used to map a numeric signal to its symbolic name and to validate membership.
  • signal.valid_signals() — returns the set of valid signal numbers on the platform, used to bound and validate the requested number.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"signalnum":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["signalnum"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"signalnum":{"type":"integer"},"name":{"type":["string","null"]},"description":{"type":["string","null"]},"valid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["signalnum","name","description","valid"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only and side-effect free: no signal handlers are installed, no signals are sent, no signal masks are modified, and no timers are set. Only queries strsignal, Signals and valid_signals.

Constraints Must run in the main thread of the main interpreter for any handler-related operations, though this operation itself only reads. Signal availability is platform-specific: many SIG* names are Unix-only, Windows supports only a subset (SIGABRT, SIGFPE, SIGILL, SIGINT, SIGSEGV, SIGTERM, SIGBREAK), and on WebAssembly signals are emulated with several functions/signals unavailable. SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot be caught, blocked or ignored. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError if signalnum is not a valid signal number on the platform (propagated from strsignal).
  • TypeError if signalnum is not an integer.
  • signalnum not present in signal.Signals enum: name returned as null while description may still be available.
  • Platform-dependent absence of a given SIG* constant (AttributeError if code references a name not defined on the system).

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders validating and labeling signal numbers before wiring any handler logic, using strsignal and Signals for human-readable names.
  2. Diagnostic tooling that maps raw signal numbers from logs or crash reports to symbolic names and descriptions.
  3. Cross-platform capability gating: checking valid_signals() to decide which signal-based features a builder may expose on a given platform.
  4. Documentation/help generation that enumerates Signals members with their strsignal descriptions.
  5. Input sanitization for higher-level signal-handling capabilities, rejecting invalid signal numbers early with clear errors.

Python Runtime Services

Inspect sitecustomize startup customization state for a given interpreter prefix without importing or executing sitecustomize: resolve the candidate sitecustomize module location on sys.path and report whether it is importable, using site.getsitepackages() and importlib.util.find_spec() to locate it without executing it.

  • site.getsitepackages
  • importlib.util.find_spec

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"prefixes":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional list of prefix directories to compute site-packages paths from; defaults to site.PREFIXES when omitted."},"module_name":{"type":"string","enum":["sitecustomize"],"default":"sitecustomize"}},"required":[],"additionalProperties":false}

APIs

  • sqlite3.connect(database, *, timeout=5.0, detect_types=0, isolation_level='DEFERRED', check_same_thread=True, factory=Connection, cached_statements=128, uri=False, autocommit=LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL)

  • Cursor.execute(sql, parameters=(), /)
  • Cursor.fetchall()
  • Connection.commit()
  • Connection.close()

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"database":{"type":"string","description":"Path to the SQLite database file, or \u0027:memory:\u0027 for an in-memory database."},"sql":{"type":"string","description":"A single SQL statement using qmark or named placeholders."},"parameters":{"type":["array","object"],"description":"Sequence for unnamed placeholders or object for named placeholders.","items":{}},"timeout":{"type":"number","description":"Seconds to wait on a locked table before raising OperationalError."},"readOnly":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, do not commit; intended for SELECT-only statements."}},"required":["database","sql"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"rows":{"type":"array","description":"Fetched result rows, each row a JSON array of column values.","items":{"type":"array","items":{}}},"rowCount":{"type":"integer","description":"Number of rows returned."},"committed":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether a commit was performed."}},"required":["rows","rowCount","committed"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Opens a file or in-memory SQLite database, may create the database file if absent, may implicitly open a transaction for DML statements, and may write changes to disk when committed. No network access; no external server process.

Constraints sqlite3 is an optional CPython module requiring the third-party SQLite library; availability depends on the Python build/distributor. All connect() parameters except database are keyword-only as of Python 3.15. check_same_thread defaults to True, restricting cross-thread use. Loadable extension support is not built by default. autocommit defaults to LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL and is slated to change. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on a worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • OperationalError when the database file cannot be opened or a table remains locked beyond timeout
  • OperationalError when the SQL references missing tables or columns
  • ProgrammingError when sql contains more than one statement
  • ProgrammingError when named placeholders are used with a sequence of parameters
  • IntegrityError when a constraint (e.g. UNIQUE, NOT NULL) is violated
  • DatabaseError for malformed SQL or invalid serialized data
  • InterfaceError when the connection or cursor is already closed
  • OverflowError if bound integer values exceed SQLite's 64-bit range

Ranked use cases

  1. Run a bounded parameterized SELECT/INSERT against a local SQLite file to persist structured records for a capability builder
  2. Prototype data storage for an application before porting to a server database such as PostgreSQL

  5. Inspect sqlite_master to verify schema creation during setup or migration steps

{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"},"port":{"type":"integer"},"protocol_version":{"type":["string","null"]},"cipher":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"protocol":{"type":"string"},"bits":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["name","protocol","bits"],"additionalProperties":false},"peer_certificate":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"subject":{"type":"array"},"issuer":{"type":"array"},"subjectAltName":{"type":"array"},"notBefore":{"type":"string"},"notAfter":{"type":"string"},"notBefore_epoch":{"type":["integer","null"]},"notAfter_epoch":{"type":["integer","null"]},"serialNumber":{"type":"string"},"version":{"type":"integer"}},"additionalProperties":true},"verified_chain_length":{"type":"integer"},"unverified_chain_length":{"type":"integer"},"peer_certificate_der_base64":{"type":["string","null"]}},"required":["host","port","protocol_version","cipher","peer_certificate","verified_chain_length","unverified_chain_length"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only network egress: opens a TCP connection to the requested host and port, performs a TLS handshake, and closes the socket. No application data is sent. No files are written; certificate material is returned in-memory only. May be logged by the remote server as an inbound TLS connection.

Constraints Requires the optional ssl module built against OpenSSL 1.1.1 or newer (PEP 644); not available on WASI. Behavior and available protocol versions/ciphers depend on the linked OpenSSL version and platform socket APIs. Default context enables CERT_REQUIRED, check_hostname, VERIFY_X509_STRICT and VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN, so some legacy certificates will be rejected. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

  • SSLCertVerificationError (verify_code, verify_message) when the peer certificate chain or hostname fails validation
  • SSLError with library and reason mnemonics for handshake or protocol failures
  • socket.timeout / TimeoutError when the connection or handshake exceeds timeout_seconds
  • socket.gaierror for unresolvable host names
  • ConnectionRefusedError / OSError for unreachable or refused endpoints
  • ValueError from getpeercert() if the handshake has not completed
  • ssl.SSLEOFError or ssl.SSLZeroReturnError if the peer closes abruptly or cleanly mid-handshake
  • FileNotFoundError or ssl.SSLError when cafile/capath/cadata cannot be loaded

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight TLS posture audit of internal service endpoints before deploying capability workers that must reach them
  2. Certificate expiry and chain-completeness monitoring for services consumed by automation pipelines
  3. Verifying that a custom CA bundle (cafile/capath/cadata) correctly validates a target host before wiring it into a client context
  4. Recording negotiated protocol version and cipher for compliance evidence and downgrade detection
  5. Diagnosing hostname/SAN mismatches by comparing subjectAltName entries against the requested server_hostname

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"mode":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Raw st_mode integer from os.stat/os.fstat/os.lstat"}},"required":["mode"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"fileType":{"type":"string","enum":["directory","regular","symlink","char_device","block_device","fifo","socket","other"]},"typeBits":{"type":"integer","description":"Result of stat.S_IFMT(mode)"},"permissionBits":{"type":"integer","description":"Result of stat.S_IMODE(mode)"},"filemode":{"type":"string","description":"Result of stat.filemode(mode), e.g. \u0027-rwxrwxrwx\u0027"}},"required":["fileType","typeBits","permissionBits","filemode"],"additionalProperties":false}

Text Processing Services

Python documentation

Render a bounded, validated $-template substitution using string.Template.safe_substitute, returning the rendered text plus the identifiers that were resolved and the identifiers left unresolved, without raising on missing placeholders.

APIs

  • string.Template
  • string.Template.safe_substitute
  • string.Template.get_identifiers
  • string.Template.is_valid
  • string.capwords

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"template":{"type":"string","description":"Template text using $-placeholders ($$, $name, ${name})."},"mapping":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Placeholder name to replacement string."},"capitalize_words":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, apply string.capwords to the rendered result."}},"required":["template","mapping"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"rendered":{"type":"string"},"resolved":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"unresolved":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"valid":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["rendered","resolved","unresolved","valid"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory string transformation; no filesystem, network, locale mutation, or global state changes. Does not call locale.setlocale, so 'n' formatting behavior is unaffected. No installation or execution is claimed.

Constraints Standard library only; no third-party dependencies. Behavior is locale-independent for the constants and Template class. safe_substitute never raises on missing placeholders or stray '$', so callers must inspect unresolved/valid. Output size should be bounded by the caller. Platform-neutral across CPython 3.x supporting get_identifiers/is_valid (3.11+).

Failure modes

  • Input fails JSON Schema validation (missing template or mapping, non-string values).
  • Template contains a malformed placeholder; safe_substitute leaves it intact rather than raising, so validity is reported via the valid field (is_valid returns false).
  • Mapping values are non-string and cannot be coerced; rejected at schema validation.
  • Rendered output exceeds a configured size bound; operation must reject rather than truncate silently.
  • capitalize_words applied to non-ASCII text may produce locale-independent but unexpected casing per str.capitalize semantics.

Ranked use cases

  1. Safe i18n message rendering where missing translations must degrade gracefully instead of raising KeyError.
  2. Configuration/notification templating for pipeline tooling that must report which placeholders were unresolved.
  3. Pre-flight validation of user-authored templates before committing them to a render step.
  4. Batch generation of human-readable labels from structured records with deterministic, locale-independent output.

{"type":"object","properties":{"template":{"type":"object","description":"A Template instance (or structurally equivalent object exposing strings and interpolations)"},"strict":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, reject interpolations whose format_spec is not accepted by format(); if false, fall back to str(value)","default":true}},"required":["template"]}

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"format":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"struct format string, e.g. \u0027\u003C10sHHb\u0027"},"values":{"type":"array","description":"Positional values matching the format; ints, floats, bools, bytes, bytearray, or complex per format characters","items":{}},"expectedSize":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional expected byte size; if provided must equal calcsize(format)"}},"required":["format","values"],"additionalProperties":false}

This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

  • struct.error raised for malformed format strings (bad format character, invalid repeat count, whitespace inside a count)
  • struct.error raised when the number of values does not match the format
  • struct.error raised when an integer value is outside the valid range for its format character (e.g. 'h' requires -32768 <= number <= 32767)
  • struct.error raised when a value type is incompatible with its format character (e.g. non-bytes for 's'/'c', non-numeric for numeric codes)
  • struct.error raised when 'n', 'N', or 'P' are used with a non-native byte-order prefix ('=', '<', '>', '!')
  • Size mismatch error when expectedSize is supplied and differs from calcsize(format)
  • Input validation error when format is empty or values is not an array

  1. Packing fixed-layout binary records (e.g. '<10sHHb' student records) for file or network interchange with explicit byte order
  2. Encoding network-order headers and protocol fields using '!' big-endian formats for wire-format messages
  3. Serializing numeric arrays or sensor samples into compact binary blobs for storage or transport
  4. Building and validating C-compatible struct layouts in native mode for interop with compiled extensions
  5. Producing deterministic test fixtures of packed bytes for parser and decoder test suites

POSIX-only semantics for negative returncodes and signal termination; Windows kill() aliases terminate(). preexec_fn is unsafe with threads and unsupported in subinterpreters. shell=True is deliberately excluded from this binding to avoid injection. Executable path resolution differs between POSIX (cwd/env affect PATH) and Windows (they do not); fully qualified paths recommended. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • OSError (e.g. FileNotFoundError, PermissionError) when the executable cannot be spawned; surfaced as a structured error, not a returncode.
  • subprocess.TimeoutExpired when timeoutSeconds elapses; child is killed and waited for, then reported with timedOut=true and returncode from the killed process.
  • ValueError from subprocess.run for invalid argument combinations (e.g. conflicting stdin/input or capture_output with explicit stdout/stderr).
  • UnicodeDecodeError when captured bytes are not valid in the requested encoding.
  • Non-zero exit codes are returned as data (check=False), not raised; callers must inspect returncode.
  • Output buffered in memory by communicate(); large or unbounded child output risks memory exhaustion.

Ranked use cases

  1. Bounded health-check probe: run a diagnostic binary with a short timeout and capture its exit code and output for status reporting.
  2. Deterministic build-step invocation: execute a compiler or formatter with an explicit argv and environment, capturing stdout/stderr for logs.
  3. Sandboxed tool wrapper: run an untrusted-argument CLI without a shell, enforcing a timeout and returning structured results instead of exceptions.
  4. Pipeline data transform: pipe text into a filter process via stdinText and collect transformed stdout for downstream processing.
  5. Regression harness primitive: invoke a test binary, record returncode and captured streams as JSON for later comparison.

symtable

Python Language Services

Python documentation

Analyze a Python source string with symtable.symtable and return a bounded, flattened summary of the top-level symbol table: table type, name, line number, identifiers, and per-symbol scope flags, without recursing into children beyond a configurable depth limit.

APIs

  • symtable.symtable(code, filename, compile_type, *, module=None) — generates the top-level SymbolTable from source; the entry point for the operation
  • SymbolTable.get_type() — returns the SymbolTableType of a table, used to label each summarized table
  • SymbolTable.get_name() — returns the table name ('top' for modules), used as a stable label
  • SymbolTable.get_lineno() — returns the first line of the block, used for source location
  • SymbolTable.get_identifiers() — returns the names of symbols in the table, used to enumerate symbols
  • SymbolTable.lookup(name) — returns a Symbol for a name, used to read per-symbol flags
  • Symbol.is_local()/is_global()/is_nonlocal()/is_free()/is_parameter()/is_assigned()/is_referenced()/is_imported()/is_annotated()/is_namespace() — per-symbol scope classification flags
  • SymbolTable.get_children() — returns nested tables, used only up to the depth limit

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"code":{"type":"string","description":"Python source text to analyze"},"filename":{"type":"string","description":"Name reported for the code, used in diagnostics"},"compile_type":{"type":"string","enum":["exec","eval","single"],"description":"Mode passed to symtable.symtable"},"module":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional module name for warning filtering (Python 3.15\u002B)"},"max_depth":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":8,"description":"Maximum nesting depth of child tables to summarize"}},"required":["code","filename","compile_type"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"tables":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"type":{"type":"string"},"name":{"type":"string"},"lineno":{"type":"integer"},"depth":{"type":"integer"},"identifiers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},"symbols":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"is_local":{"type":"boolean"},"is_global":{"type":"boolean"},"is_nonlocal":{"type":"boolean"},"is_free":{"type":"boolean"},"is_parameter":{"type":"boolean"},"is_assigned":{"type":"boolean"},"is_referenced":{"type":"boolean"},"is_imported":{"type":"boolean"},"is_annotated":{"type":"boolean"},"is_namespace":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["name","is_local","is_global","is_nonlocal","is_free","is_parameter","is_assigned","is_referenced","is_imported","is_annotated","is_namespace"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["type","name","lineno","depth","identifiers","symbols"],"additionalProperties":false}},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"table_count":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["tables","truncated","table_count"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints Requires a CPython runtime providing the symtable module; behavior and available SymbolTableType members vary by Python version (annotation/type-alias/type-parameter types added in 3.12–3.13, is_cell and get_cells in 3.15, module parameter in 3.15). SymbolTable and Symbol constructors are not public, so only the documented factory and accessors are used. Class.get_methods is deprecated since 3.14 and is not used. Output is bounded by max_depth and internal size caps. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

  • ValueError from compile_type not in {exec, eval, single}
  • TypeError when code or filename is not a string
  • ValueError from SymbolTable.lookup if a name is absent (guarded internally; reported as internal inconsistency)
  • Recursion or size limits exceeded when max_depth or symbol counts exceed configured bounds; result marked truncated
  • UnicodeDecodeError if source is supplied as bytes rather than str (rejected by input schema)

Ranked use cases

  1. Static scope analysis for capability builders: classify identifiers as local/global/free/parameter to reason about name resolution before generating or transforming code
  2. Pre-flight validation of generated Python snippets: detect syntax errors and unexpected global/nonlocal declarations before handing code to an executor
  3. Closure and cell detection for dependency extraction: identify free and cell variables to determine what context a function needs
  4. Import and namespace auditing: flag imported names and namespace-introducing bindings to build module dependency maps
  5. Annotation and type-scope inspection: enumerate annotated symbols and type-parameter scopes to support typing-aware tooling

Python documentation

Claim a monitoring tool identifier and atomically configure its global event mask and per-code-object local event mask, returning the prior configuration so a capability builder can restore it.

APIs

  • sys.monitoring.use_tool_id
  • sys.monitoring.get_tool
  • sys.monitoring.get_events
  • sys.monitoring.set_events

  • sys.monitoring.events

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"tool_id":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":5},"tool_name":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"global_event_mask":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"local_events":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"code":{"type":"object"},"event_mask":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}},"required":["code","event_mask"]}},"restore_on_release":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["tool_id","tool_name","global_event_mask"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"tool_id":{"type":"integer"},"tool_name":{"type":"string"},"previous_global_event_mask":{"type":"integer"},"applied_global_event_mask":{"type":"integer"},"previous_local_events":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"code":{"type":"object"},"event_mask":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["code","event_mask"]}},"restore_token":{"type":"string"}},"required":["tool_id","tool_name","previous_global_event_mask","applied_global_event_mask","previous_local_events","restore_token"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Mutates process-global interpreter monitoring state: claims a tool identifier, changes the global event mask and per-code-object local event masks for that tool. No callbacks are registered, so no user code is invoked. State persists until released via free_tool_id or restored via restore_token.

Requires CPython 3.12+ (clear_tool_id and per-code-object disabling of other events require 3.14/3.15). Tool identifiers are limited to 0..5 and are process-wide, so concurrent tools must coordinate.   • Auditing event sys.monitoring.register_callback is not raised here since no callbacks are registered by this operation

  1. Coverage tool bootstrap: claim COVERAGE_ID and enable LINE plus PY_START/PY_RETURN masks per code object for a bounded measurement window.
  2. Debugger breakpoint setup: claim DEBUGGER_ID, enable LINE globally, and rely on DISABLE returns to keep overhead near zero outside breakpoints.

  4. Test-harness instrumentation guard: verify a tool id is free via get_tool before claiming, preventing collisions between parallel capability builders.

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"sent":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if syslog.syslog() returned without raising."},"priority":{"type":"integer","description":"Numeric priority value passed to syslog() (facility|level)."},"openlogCalled":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether this operation invoked openlog() before sending."},"messageLength":{"type":"integer","description":"Length of the message string as submitted (before any newline addition)."}},"required":["sent","priority","openlogCalled","messageLength"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Sends one message to the host system logger; may implicitly trigger openlog() with no arguments if the log is not open; may change module-level ident/logoption/facility state if ident or logoption is supplied; emits auditing events syslog.openlog and syslog.syslog. No files are written by the binding itself and no network I/O is performed directly.

Constraints Unix only; not available on WASI or iOS. Requires a working system syslog facility. openlog()/closelog()/setlogmask() are restricted to the main interpreter in Python 3.12+. Facility and log-option constants depend on availability (LOG_AUTHPRIV, LOG_FTP, LOG_NETINFO, LOG_REMOTEAUTH, LOG_INSTALL, LOG_RAS, LOG_LAUNCHD, LOG_ODELAY, LOG_NOWAIT, LOG_PERROR). This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • RuntimeError when syslog() is called in a subinterpreter before openlog() was called in the main interpreter (Python 3.12+ restriction)
  • RuntimeError when openlog() is called in a subinterpreter (main-interpreter-only restriction)
  • ValueError/TypeError for a non-string message or invalid priority value
  • OSError from the underlying system syslog routines (e.g. unavailable or misconfigured syslog daemon)
  • Auditing hook may raise, aborting the call before the message is sent
  • Message silently dropped by the system logger if the active setlogmask() mask excludes the priority level

Ranked use cases

  1. Emit a single structured operational event (e.g. job start/failure) to the host syslog with an explicit level and facility for centralized log collection.
  2. Tag messages with a stable ident and LOG_PID so multi-process workers can be correlated in syslog output.
  3. Route messages to a dedicated facility (e.g. LOG_LOCAL0) to separate application logs from system logs in downstream pipelines.
  4. Provide a minimal, auditable logging primitive for capability builders that must integrate with existing Unix syslog infrastructure rather than a Python logging handler.
  5. Send high-severity alerts (LOG_ERR/LOG_CRIT) from long-running services without pulling in the full logging framework.

Create a securely-named temporary directory scoped to a single bounded call, returning its absolute path and a cleanup token, without performing any cleanup itself (cleanup is a separate explicit step).

  • tempfile.mkdtemp(suffix=None, prefix=None, dir=None)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"prefix":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Filename prefix; null uses module default"},"suffix":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Filename suffix; null means no suffix"},"dir":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Parent directory; null uses gettempdir()"}},"required":["prefix","suffix","dir"],"additionalProperties":false}

{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute pathname of the created directory"},"parent":{"type":"string","description":"Directory in which it was created"},"cleanupToken":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque token identifying this directory for a later explicit cleanup step"}},"required":["path","parent","cleanupToken"],"additionalProperties":false}

No cleanup is performed by this operation; the directory persists until an explicit cleanup step removes it. Raises the tempfile.mkdtemp auditing event with the full path. Behavior depends on interpreter version and on whether the callable is importable in the current process. Not available on non-CPython implementations. No installation or availability on any worker is claimed.

Failure modes

  • callableRef does not resolve to a callable: raise ValueError before entering capture
  • callable raises an exception: capture is exited cleanly, exception type reported in 'raised', warnings still returned
  • category is not a Warning subclass or cannot be imported: raise ValueError
  • callable returns a non-JSON-serializable object: raise TypeError on serialization
  • warnings filter state cannot be restored: propagate underlying exception

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders can wrap third-party code to inventory which DeprecationWarning/ResourceWarning categories it emits before upgrading dependencies.
  2. Regression harnesses can record warning output of a function as structured JSON for diffing across interpreter versions.
  3. Test authors can convert ad-hoc warning assertions into data-driven checks by inspecting captured categories and messages.
  4. Library maintainers can audit that a code path emits no unexpected warnings under a strict 'error' filter.
  5. Tooling can surface warning provenance (filename/lineno) to pinpoint deprecated call sites in vendored code.

timeit.repeat: run a bounded, repeated timing of a small statement with a fixed setup and explicit repeat/number counts, returning the raw per-repetition durations in seconds

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"stmt":{"type":"string","description":"Statement to time; may contain multiple statements separated by ; or newlines"},"setup":{"type":"string","description":"Statement executed once before timing; defaults to \u0027pass\u0027"},"repeat":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Number of timing repetitions"},"number":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Executions of stmt per repetition"},"use_process_time":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, use time.process_time() instead of time.perf_counter()"}},"required":["stmt","repeat","number"],"additionalProperties":false}

Parse a bounded TOML document string into a Python dict via tomllib.loads, with a caller-supplied maximum input size and optional float parser selection, returning the decoded mapping or a structured decode error.

APIs

  • tomllib.loads(s, /, *, parse_float=float) — parses a TOML str and returns a dict; the core operation of this binding.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"toml_text":{"type":"string","description":"TOML document to parse."},"max_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"description":"Upper bound on UTF-8 encoded size of toml_text; enforced before parsing."},"parse_float":{"type":"string","enum":["float","decimal"],"default":"float","description":"Float decoding strategy; \u0027decimal\u0027 maps to decimal.Decimal."}},"required":["toml_text","max_bytes"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"ok":{"type":"boolean"},"data":{"type":["object","null"],"description":"Decoded TOML document as a mapping; null when ok is false."},"error":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"type":{"type":"string","enum":["TOMLDecodeError","SizeLimitExceeded","InvalidFloatParserResult"]},"msg":{"type":"string"},"pos":{"type":["integer","null"]},"lineno":{"type":["integer","null"]},"colno":{"type":["integer","null"]}},"required":["type","msg"],"additionalProperties":false}},"required":["ok","data","error"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints Requires Python 3.11+ (TOML 1.0.0); TOML 1.1.0 support requires Python 3.15+. Read-only: no serialization/writing. Integer parsing subject to Python's int string conversion limit (default 4300 digits). Floats default to binary64. Nesting bounded by recursion limit. Callers must enforce size limits for untrusted input. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • TOMLDecodeError raised for syntactically invalid TOML; mapped to error.type='TOMLDecodeError' with msg/pos/lineno/colno.
  • SizeLimitExceeded when UTF-8 encoded toml_text exceeds max_bytes; parsing is not attempted.
  • InvalidFloatParserResult (ValueError) when the configured float parser returns a dict or list.
  • RecursionError possible for deeply nested arrays/tables, since nesting is mainly limited by Python's recursion limit.
  • Resource exhaustion (CPU/memory) on adversarial input even within size limits; documentation warns to bound input size.
  • UnicodeEncodeError if toml_text cannot be encoded as UTF-8 for size measurement.

Ranked use cases

  1. Safely parse untrusted pyproject.toml-style configuration strings with an enforced byte-size cap before decoding.
  2. Decode TOML configuration into a dict for downstream validation, using decimal.Decimal for lossless float handling.
  3. Surface precise TOML syntax errors (line/column) to users editing configuration files.
  4. Convert TOML documents into Python-native structures for round-tripping into other config formats.

Effects Pure in-memory computation; no file, network or subprocess side effects. Does not mutate the exception. When capture_locals=true, reads local variable reprs (potential information disclosure). Does not clear frames; caller may separately invoke traceback.clear_frames to release references.

Constraints Requires a live in-process exception object; cannot accept a serialized/pickled exception across process boundaries. TracebackException avoids holding frame/traceback references, but capture_locals=true retains stringified locals only. Behavior of limit differs from sys.tracebacklimit. show_group and max_group_* require Python 3.11+; compact requires 3.10+; exc_type_str requires 3.13+.   • limit is not an integer or null -> TypeError
  • max_group_width/max_group_depth out of range or non-integer -> ValueError/TypeError

  • capture_locals=true may expose sensitive local values in output

Ranked use cases

  1. Structured error reporting: convert caught exceptions into bounded, JSON-serializable traceback text for logs/telemetry without leaking frame references.
  2. Long-lived error storage: capture exception details at raise time and format later (e.g., deferred reporting) using TracebackException to avoid retaining large object graphs.
  3. Exception-group diagnostics: render nested BaseExceptionGroup trees with bounded width/depth for aggregated task failures.
  4. Debug tooling: optional capture_locals to include local variable snapshots in developer-facing tracebacks.
  5. Chained-exception analysis: toggle chain to include or suppress __cause__/__context__ for root-cause vs. surface-error views.

Effects Read-only with respect to application data. May start tracemalloc tracing (installs allocator hooks, adding CPU/memory overhead) if not already active and permitted. May reset the recorded peak size when reset_peak=True. May write a snapshot file to dump_snapshot_path. Does not clear existing traces unless tracing is stopped elsewhere. No network access.

Tracing should ideally be started at interpreter startup via PYTHONTRACEMALLOC or -X tracemalloc=NFRAME for full coverage; runtime start() misses earlier allocations. Snapshot files are version-specific and not portable across Python versions. Storing more frames increases overhead. Not available on builds without tracemalloc support. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

  • TracingNotStarted: tracemalloc.is_tracing() is False and start() was not permitted, so take_snapshot() cannot run.
  • InvalidKeyType: key_type not in {filename, lineno, traceback}.

  • InvalidLimit: limit outside 1..1000.
  • BaselineLoadError: baseline_snapshot_path unreadable, not a valid tracemalloc dump, or produced by an incompatible Python version.
  • DumpWriteError: dump_snapshot_path not writable or disk full.
  • FilterError: malformed fnmatch pattern in include/exclude patterns.
  • TracebackLimitError: get_traceback_limit() raises because tracing is not active.
  • MemoryPressure: snapshotting a large heap may itself consume significant memory; bounded by limit and by refusing when get_tracemalloc_memory() exceeds a configured cap.

Ranked use cases

  1. Leak triage in long-running services: compare a baseline dump against a fresh snapshot to surface the top growing allocation sites by line number.
  2. CI memory-regression gate: capture top-N statistics per test run and fail when size_diff for a tracked file exceeds a threshold.
  3. Hot-path allocation profiling: identify the highest-volume allocation lines to target for optimization (e.g., replacing list(range(...)) with range(...)).
  4. Peak-memory auditing of batch jobs: reset_peak before a phase, then report current vs peak traced bytes alongside top allocators.
  5. Offline forensic analysis: dump snapshots from a constrained environment and reload them elsewhere for statistics and traceback inspection.

{"type":"object","properties":{"class_ref":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted import path of the class to introspect, e.g. \u0027collections.OrderedDict\u0027."},"include_resolved":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether to also compute the resolved bases via resolve_bases.","default":true}},"required":["class_ref"],"additionalProperties":false}

  • AttributeError when the final path segment is not an attribute of the resolved module/object.

  1. Verify that a collaborator method is invoked exactly once with expected arguments during a unit test of a capability builder's orchestration code.
  2. Isolate a capability builder from network or filesystem dependencies by substituting a mock for an I/O client and asserting call patterns.
  3. Capture the ordered sequence of calls a builder makes to a dependency to validate control flow and ordering.
  4. Inject deterministic return values into a dependency to exercise downstream branches without real side effects.
  5. Provide a structured, JSON-serializable audit of mock interactions for reporting in automated test harnesses.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"URL string to split; may be relative or absolute."},"default_scheme":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Scheme to use only if the URL does not specify one."},"allow_fragments":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If false, fragment identifiers are not recognized and are parsed as part of path or query."},"missing_as_none":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, absent components are returned as null instead of empty strings."}},"required":["url"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"scheme":{"type":["string","null"]},"netloc":{"type":["string","null"]},"path":{"type":["string","null"]},"query":{"type":["string","null"]},"fragment":{"type":["string","null"]},"username":{"type":["string","null"]},"password":{"type":["string","null"]},"hostname":{"type":["string","null"]},"port":{"type":["integer","null"]},"normalized_url":{"type":"string"}},"required":["scheme","netloc","path","query","fragment","username","password","hostname","port","normalized_url"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory string parsing; no network access, no file I/O, no mutation of external state. Leading C0 control and space characters are stripped and \n, \r and \t are removed from the input before parsing, so the reported normalized_url may differ from the raw input.

Constraints Requires a CPython 3.x runtime providing urllib.parse; the missing_as_none parameter requires Python 3.15 or later, so on earlier runtimes it must be emulated or rejected. Behavior is not fully RFC 3986 or WHATWG compliant and is not a validator. The itms-services scheme handling may be removed on iOS and optionally on macOS builds. No installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

  • ValueError raised when the netloc contains unmatched square brackets.
  • ValueError raised when reading the port attribute if an invalid or out-of-range port is specified.
  • ValueError raised when netloc characters decompose under NFKC normalization into '/', '?', '#', '@' or ':'.
  • TypeError raised if str and bytes/bytearray data are mixed in a single call.
  • UnicodeDecodeError raised if non-ASCII byte values are passed in byte input.

Ranked use cases

  1. Splitting user-supplied or configuration-supplied URLs into scheme, host, path and query for routing, logging or allowlist checks before any fetch.
  2. Extracting hostname and port from a URL to build connection targets or to compare against a permitted-host set.
  3. Separating query and fragment from a URL so the query can be handed to parse_qs and the fragment handled separately.
  4. Normalizing a URL via geturl for deduplication or cache keys while preserving the original components.
  5. Diagnosing malformed URLs by surfacing ValueError conditions such as bad ports or unmatched brackets in netloc.

Python documentation

fetch_url_metadata: perform a single bounded HTTP(S) GET via urllib.request.urlopen with an explicit timeout, read at most a capped number of response bytes, and return status, headers, and a truncated body preview without following unbounded redirects or retries.

APIs

  • urllib.request.urlopen(url, data=None, timeout, *, context=None) — opens the URL and returns a context-manager response object exposing url, headers, and status
  • urllib.request.Request(url, data=None, headers={}, method=None) — constructs the request abstraction used to set method and headers
  • urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler — handler class governing redirect behavior within an opener chain
  • urllib.request.build_opener([handler, ...]) — assembles an OpenerDirector chaining handlers for controlled request behavior

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute, properly encoded http or https URL"},"timeoutSeconds":{"type":"number","minimum":0.1,"maximum":120,"description":"Blocking timeout for connection and read"},"maxBytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":1048576,"description":"Maximum number of response body bytes to read"},"headers":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional request headers"},"method":{"type":"string","enum":["GET","HEAD"],"description":"HTTP method; defaults to GET"}},"required":["url","timeoutSeconds","maxBytes"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"integer","description":"HTTP status code"},"finalUrl":{"type":"string","description":"URL of the response after any redirects"},"headers":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"description":"Response headers as name/value strings"},"bodyPreview":{"type":"string","description":"Decoded (utf-8, errors=replace) prefix of the body"},"bytesRead":{"type":"integer","description":"Number of body bytes actually read"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean","description":"True if body exceeded maxBytes"}},"required":["status","finalUrl","headers","bodyPreview","bytesRead","truncated"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Performs outbound network I/O to the target host (or configured proxy) and reads a bounded amount of response data; emits the urllib.Request auditing event with fullurl, data, headers, and method; may consult proxy environment variables and system proxy settings; no filesystem writes and no persistent state beyond any installed global opener.

Constraints Availability: not WASI (does not work on WebAssembly). On macOS, unsafe in programs using os.fork() because getproxies() uses a higher-level system API; set no_proxy='*' to avoid. Uses HTTP/1.1 and sends Connection: close. Timeout applies only to HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP connections. HTTPS requires ssl module support; custom SSLContext should set ALPN protocols. HTTP_PROXY is ignored when REQUEST_METHOD is set (CGI). Redirects to non-HTTP/HTTPS/FTP URLs raise HTTPError as a security measure. Data objects that cannot be re-delivered may fail on redirect or auth retry; no 100-continue support.

Failure modes

  • URLError raised on protocol errors (e.g., connection refused, DNS failure, unsupported scheme)
  • ValueError raised if url is not a valid URL
  • TimeoutError (OSError subclass) if the server does not respond within timeoutSeconds
  • http.client.RemoteDisconnected if the server closes the connection without a response
  • http.client.BadStatusLine and other http.client.HTTPException subclasses propagate unchanged (not wrapped in URLError)
  • HTTPError raised for non-2xx responses when default error handling is in effect
  • ValueError from DataHandler on malformed base64 data URLs with missing padding
  • URLError from FileHandler when a remote hostname is given for a file URL
  • URLError from url2pathname when authority cannot be resolved on non-Windows platforms

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders probing endpoint reachability and status codes with strict timeouts and byte caps for safe health checks
  2. Fetching small API or metadata documents (JSON/HTML head) for content extraction pipelines with bounded memory use
  3. Validating redirect chains and final URLs for link-integrity auditing without unbounded following
  4. Retrieving headers only (HEAD) to inspect content type, length, and caching directives before deciding to download
  5. Testing proxy and authentication handler configurations in a controlled opener chain for network diagnostics

Parse a caller-supplied robots.txt document (as a list of text lines) with urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser.parse and answer a single bounded query for one user agent: whether a given URL may be fetched, plus the applicable crawl delay, request rate and sitemap list.   • urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser.can_fetch(useragent, url) — returns True/False for whether the user agent may fetch the URL
  • urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser.crawl_delay(useragent) — returns the Crawl-delay value or None
  • urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser.request_rate(useragent) — returns RequestRate(requests, seconds) named tuple or None
  • urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser.site_maps() — returns list of Sitemap entries or None

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"robots_txt_lines":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Lines of the robots.txt document, supplied by the caller"},"user_agent":{"type":"string","description":"User agent token to evaluate rules against"},"url":{"type":"string","description":"Absolute URL to test with can_fetch"}},"required":["robots_txt_lines","user_agent","url"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"can_fetch":{"type":"boolean"},"crawl_delay":{"type":["number","null"]},"request_rate":{"type":["object","null"],"properties":{"requests":{"type":"integer"},"seconds":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["requests","seconds"],"additionalProperties":false},"site_maps":{"type":["array","null"],"items":{"type":"string"}}},"required":["can_fetch","crawl_delay","request_rate","site_maps"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory parsing and querying; no network access, no file writes, no persistent state. The parser instance is local to the operation.

Constraints Requires a Python runtime providing urllib.robotparser (documented as available in Python 3.15.2 docs). Caller must obtain robots.txt content by other means; this operation does not fetch it. Behavior follows RFC 9309 as implemented by the module. No claim of installation, availability on any worker, or execution is made.

Failure modes

  • Invalid or malformed robots.txt lines are tolerated by the parser; unrecognized directives are ignored rather than raising
  • crawl_delay returns None when the parameter is absent, inapplicable to the user agent, or syntactically invalid
  • request_rate returns None when the parameter is absent, inapplicable, or syntactically invalid
  • site_maps returns None when no Sitemap entry exists or entries are invalid
  • can_fetch may raise on a malformed URL argument
  • No network errors occur because read() is not used; callers must supply the document text themselves

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight crawl permission check for a URL before a spider fetches it, using a robots.txt document already retrieved
  2. Rate-limit planning: extract crawl_delay and request_rate for a user agent to schedule polite request pacing
  3. Sitemap discovery: extract Sitemap entries from a robots.txt document for downstream indexing pipelines
  4. Compliance auditing: batch-evaluate a set of URLs against a stored robots.txt to flag disallowed paths
  5. Test harness for robots.txt rule evaluation without network dependency, using fixture documents

Internet Protocols and Support

Python documentation

Generate a single UUID of a caller-selected version (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8) and return its canonical string form plus parsed metadata (version, variant, hex, urn, int, is_safe), with namespace/name required only for versions 3 and 5.

APIs

  • uuid.uuid4() — generates a cryptographically-secure random UUID (RFC 9562 §5.4); used as the default version when none is requested.
  • uuid.uuid5(namespace, name) — generates a deterministic SHA-1-based UUID from a namespace UUID and a name; used when version 5 is requested.
  • uuid.UUID — immutable UUID object exposing .hex, .urn, .int, .version, .variant, .is_safe; used to normalize and report the generated value.
  • uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS / NAMESPACE_URL / NAMESPACE_OID / NAMESPACE_X500 — predefined namespace identifiers accepted as shorthand for versions 3 and 5.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"version":{"type":"integer","enum":[1,3,4,5,6,7,8],"default":4,"description":"UUID version to generate."},"namespace":{"type":"string","description":"Namespace UUID string or one of \u0027@dns\u0027,\u0027@url\u0027,\u0027@oid\u0027,\u0027@x500\u0027. Required when version is 3 or 5."},"name":{"type":"string","description":"Name to hash. Required when version is 3 or 5."},"node":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional 48-bit node for versions 1 and 6."},"clock_seq":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"description":"Optional 14-bit clock sequence for versions 1 and 6."}},"required":["version"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"uuid":{"type":"string","description":"Canonical 8-4-4-4-12 lowercase hex form."},"hex":{"type":"string","description":"32-character lowercase hex string."},"urn":{"type":"string","description":"URN form \u0027urn:uuid:...\u0027."},"int":{"type":"integer","description":"128-bit integer value."},"version":{"type":"integer","description":"UUID version number."},"variant":{"type":"string","description":"Variant name (e.g. \u0027RFC_4122\u0027)."},"is_safe":{"type":"string","enum":["safe","unsafe","unknown"],"description":"SafeUUID status."}},"required":["uuid","hex","urn","int","version","variant","is_safe"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-process computation; no filesystem, network, or persistent state is modified. uuid1()/uuid6() may invoke a separate program to obtain the hardware address on first call, which can be slow. No installation or execution is claimed.

Constraints Requires Python 3.14+ for versions 6, 7, 8 and for NIL/MAX; versions 1,3,4,5 available on all supported CPython 3.x. uuid1() may embed the host MAC address and thus leak privacy. uuid8() is not CSPRNG-backed by default; use uuid4() for security-sensitive identifiers. uuid3() uses MD5 and is not collision-resistant.

Failure modes

  • ValueError when version is 3 or 5 and namespace or name is missing.
  • ValueError when namespace string is not a valid UUID and not a recognized '@dns'/'@url'/'@oid'/'@x500' shorthand.
  • ValueError when version is not one of 1,3,4,5,6,7,8.
  • TypeError when name is not a string or bytes.
  • Platform-dependent behavior for uuid1()/uuid6() when getnode() cannot obtain a hardware address (falls back to random node; is_safe may be 'unknown').

Ranked use cases

  1. Deterministic idempotency keys: derive stable UUIDs from (namespace, name) via uuid5() so retried operations map to the same identifier.
  2. Database-friendly primary keys: generate time-ordered UUIDv7 (or v6) values to improve index locality in storage systems.
  3. Correlation and trace identifiers: mint random uuid4() values for request/span IDs in logging pipelines.
  4. Content-addressed references: use uuid3()/uuid5() to fingerprint named resources (URLs, DNS names, OIDs) for deduplication.
  5. Test fixtures and data seeding: produce reproducible UUIDs from fixed namespaces for deterministic test data.

weakref

Data Types

Python documentation

weakref.probe_referent: given a live weak reference handle registered in a bounded in-process registry, report whether its referent is still alive and, if so, return a stable opaque token for it, without ever resurrecting or strongly retaining the referent.

APIs

  • weakref.ref(object[, callback]) — creates the weak reference whose liveness is probed; calling it returns the referent or None
  • weakref.getweakrefcount(object) — reports how many weak references/proxies currently target the referent, used as a diagnostic field
  • weakref.getweakrefs(object) — enumerates existing weak reference and proxy objects for the referent, used to detect duplicate registration
  • weakref.finalize(obj, func, *args, **kwargs) — registers cleanup tied to referent collection so registry entries are pruned deterministically
  • weakref.WeakValueDictionary — backs the handle registry so entries vanish automatically when referents are collected

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"handle":{"type":"string","description":"Opaque handle previously issued by this operation for a registered weak reference"},"includeWeakrefCount":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, include getweakrefcount of the live referent in the result"}},"required":["handle"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"handle":{"type":"string"},"alive":{"type":"boolean"},"referentToken":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Opaque token identifying the live referent; null when not alive"},"weakrefCount":{"type":["integer","null"],"minimum":0,"description":"Present only when includeWeakrefCount was true and referent is alive"},"callbackPresent":{"type":"boolean","description":"Whether the underlying weakref has a non-None __callback__"}},"required":["handle","alive","referentToken","callbackPresent"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only with respect to the referent: the operation never creates strong references, never resurrects collected objects, and never mutates the referent. It may cause registry pruning (removal of dead entries) and, if includeWeakrefCount is requested, invokes getweakrefcount which is side-effect free. No files, network, or subprocess effects.

Constraints CPython-specific behavior for some types (tuple and int are not weak-referenceable even when subclassed). Weak reference support requires '__weakref__' in __slots__ when slots are defined. Weak references are hashable only if the referent is hashable and only before deletion. Proxies are never hashable. Finalizers are not invoked during the late interpreter-shutdown window when module globals may be None, and finalizers created in daemonic threads may not run at exit. Callbacks run from most-recently-registered to oldest. Operation must be implemented with the ref() is not None idiom to remain thread-safe. No installation, availability, or execution is claimed by this proposal.

Failure modes

  • UnknownHandle: handle not present in registry (never issued or already pruned)
  • InvalidHandleType: handle is not a string
  • ReferentNotWeakReferenceable: registration-time TypeError because the object type does not support weak references (e.g. list, dict, int, tuple, or __slots__ without '__weakref__')
  • CallbackErrorSuppressed: exceptions raised by weakref callbacks are written to stderr and cannot be propagated, so registry pruning errors are only observable out-of-band
  • HashAfterDeath: calling hash() on a weak reference first time after referent deletion raises TypeError; operation must avoid hashing dead references
  • ProxyReferenceError: if a proxy is used instead of ref, attribute access after collection raises ReferenceError; operation must use ref() is not None idiom
  • RaceOnLiveness: separate liveness test then dereference is unsafe under threads; operation must dereference once and branch on the returned value

Ranked use cases

  1. Cache liveness probe: verify whether a large cached object (e.g. image or array) is still alive before attempting reuse, enabling bounded caches that do not pin memory.
  2. Registry hygiene for object-ID maps: implement the documented id-to-object pattern with WeakValueDictionary and expose a safe probe so callers can check staleness without resurrecting objects.
  3. Finalizer lifecycle inspection: report whether a registered weakref.finalize cleanup is still pending (alive) versus already executed or detached, supporting deterministic resource teardown audits.
  4. Duplicate-reference diagnostics: use getweakrefcount/getweakrefs to detect that a referent already carries many weak references or proxies, flagging potential leaks in long-lived registries.
  5. Thread-safe observer bookkeeping: provide a single-dereference liveness check for observer/subscriber lists held weakly, avoiding the race between separate liveness tests and dereference in multithreaded code.

Python documentation

Open a single URL in the user's default browser via webbrowser.open, returning whether a browser launch was reported successful, without waiting for or controlling the browser session.

APIs

  • webbrowser.open(url, new=0, autoraise=True) — module-level convenience function that displays the URL using the default browser and returns True if a browser was successfully launched, False otherwise; raises the webbrowser.open auditing event with argument url.
  • webbrowser.Error — exception raised when a browser control error occurs, surfaced as a structured failure.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"url":{"type":"string","description":"URL (or, on some platforms, filename) to display; passed verbatim to webbrowser.open."},"new":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1,2],"default":0,"description":"0 = same window if possible, 1 = new window if possible, 2 = new tab if possible."},"autoraise":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"Raise the browser window if possible."}},"required":["url"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"launched":{"type":"boolean","description":"Value returned by webbrowser.open: True if a browser was successfully launched, False otherwise."},"url":{"type":"string","description":"Echo of the requested URL."},"new":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1,2],"description":"Echo of the requested new-window mode."}},"required":["launched","url","new"],"additionalProperties":false}

Behavior is platform-dependent: on non-Unix platforms or with a remote browser the controlling process does not wait; on Unix without a remote browser it launches and waits. BROWSER environment variable (os.pathsep-separated, %s substitution) influences browser selection and, since 3.14, can reorder platform defaults. On iOS, BROWSER, autoraise, browser preference and new tab/window arguments are ignored and ctypes is required. Opening filenames is neither supported nor portable. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • webbrowser.Error raised by the underlying browser controller; reported as a structured error rather than a boolean.
  • webbrowser.open returns False when no browser could be launched; this is a non-exception failure and must be surfaced as launched=false.
  • On iOS, calls to open() fail if the ctypes module is unavailable.
  • On Unix with only text-mode browsers, the calling process blocks until the user exits the browser, so the call may not return promptly.
  • Invalid or malformed URL strings are not validated by the module; behavior is delegated to the launched browser or OS handler.
  • Auditing event webbrowser.open may be observed or blocked by audit hooks, causing the call to fail or be denied.

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders exposing a single safe 'open documentation URL in the user's browser' action for interactive agent or assistant workflows.
  2. Local developer tooling that surfaces generated reports or artifacts (e.g., HTML output) to the user's default browser after a build step.
  3. Onboarding or help flows that open a project's documentation site in a new tab on explicit user request.
  4. Test harnesses or demos that verify browser-launch wiring by checking the boolean return of webbrowser.open without asserting on browser internals.
  5. Desktop notification or alert pipelines that deep-link the user to a relevant web console page from a local script.

{"type":"object","properties":{"environ":{"type":"object","description":"CGI-like environment mapping of string keys to string values (e.g. REQUEST_METHOD, PATH_INFO, SERVER_NAME, SERVER_PORT, SERVER_PROTOCOL).","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}},"requestBody":{"type":"string","description":"Raw request body bytes, base64-encoded, exposed as wsgi.input."},"multithread":{"type":"boolean","default":true},"multiprocess":{"type":"boolean","default":false},"appModule":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted module path of the WSGI application callable."},"appName":{"type":"string","description":"Attribute name of the WSGI application callable within appModule."}},"required":["environ","appModule","appName"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-process execution: the handler writes only to the caller-supplied stdout/stderr buffers and mutates only its own copy of environ. No sockets are opened, no files are served, and sys.stdin/sys.stdout/sys.stderr/os.environ are not read or modified. The application itself may perform arbitrary side effects and must be treated as untrusted.

BaseCGIHandler is intended for CGI-like gateway protocols and emits a Status: header rather than an HTTP status line, so output is not directly wire-ready for an origin server. The stdout object must accept full-chunk writes like io.BufferedIOBase. wsgi.run_once/multithread/multiprocess flags are set from constructor arguments.   • stdout write fails or returns short writes, violating the BufferedIOBase-style contract.

{"type":"object","properties":{"application":{"type":"object","description":"Callable WSGI application object conforming to wsgiref.types.WSGIApplication; passed by reference, not serialized"},"environ":{"type":"object","description":"WSGIEnvironment dictionary (PEP 3333); string keys, values may be str, bytes, or stream objects","additionalProperties":true},"apply_testing_defaults":{"type":"boolean","default":true,"description":"If true, fill missing keys via wsgiref.util.setup_testing_defaults before invocation"},"capture_body":{"type":"boolean","default":false,"description":"If true, collect returned body bytes (bounded) into the result"},"max_body_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"default":65536}},"required":["application","environ"],"additionalProperties":false}

  1. Safe structural inspection of untrusted XML: parse a document with a bounded event budget and return element/attribute/text summaries plus precise ExpatError line/column diagnostics for validation pipelines.

  4. Namespace-aware inventory: enumerate namespace prefix/URI bindings and expanded element names to audit XML documents for namespace hygiene.

zipapp

Software Packaging and Distribution

Python documentation

Build a bounded executable Python zip application archive from a source directory using zipapp.create_archive, optionally embedding a shebang interpreter and a generated __main__.py entry point, and report the resulting archive metadata without executing it.

APIs

  • zipapp.create_archive(source, target=None, interpreter=None, main=None, filter=None, compressed=False) — creates the application archive from a directory, file, or file object, writing the shebang line and __main__.py as specified
  • zipapp.get_interpreter(archive) — reads back the shebang interpreter from an existing archive for verification/diagnostics

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"source_dir":{"type":"string","description":"Path to a directory containing Python code to package"},"target_path":{"type":"string","description":"Output .pyz file path"},"interpreter":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Shebang interpreter command, e.g. \u0027/usr/bin/env python3\u0027; null for no shebang"},"main":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Entry point of form \u0027pkg.module:callable\u0027; null if source already contains __main__.py"},"compressed":{"type":"boolean","description":"Use deflate compression for archive members"},"include_globs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"},"description":"Optional glob patterns; only matching relative paths are included via the filter callback"}},"required":["source_dir","target_path","compressed"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"archive_path":{"type":"string"},"interpreter":{"type":["string","null"]},"main":{"type":["string","null"]},"compressed":{"type":"boolean"},"member_count":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"archive_size_bytes":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"has_main_py":{"type":"boolean"},"executable_bit_set":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["archive_path","interpreter","compressed","member_count","archive_size_bytes","has_main_py","executable_bit_set"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Writes a new .pyz file at target_path; on POSIX, sets the executable bit on the target when an interpreter is supplied. Does not execute the archive, does not import packaged code, and does not modify source_dir. Caller-supplied file objects (if used) remain caller-owned and are not closed.

Constraints Requires Python 3.5+ (filter/compressed parameters require 3.7+). C-extension dependencies cannot be loaded from inside a zip archive and must be shipped separately. Shebang portability depends on target OS and Python launcher behavior; no 'X.Y or later' interpreter syntax exists. Archive must contain __main__.py at the zip root. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • source_dir does not exist or is not a directory
  • target_path parent directory missing or not writable
  • main omitted while source_dir lacks __main__.py (archive would not be executable)
  • main specified while source_dir already contains __main__.py
  • main string not of form 'pkg.module:callable'
  • target_path equals source when copying an existing archive
  • filter callback raises or returns non-boolean
  • OSError/IOError during archive write (disk full, permission denied)
  • interpreter string contains newline or invalid shebang characters

Ranked use cases

  1. Package a directory of pure-Python application code into a single distributable .pyz with an embedded interpreter shebang for POSIX execution
  2. Generate a __main__.py entry point from a 'pkg.module:callable' spec so a source tree without one becomes a runnable archive
  3. Produce compressed standalone archives bundling vendored dependencies installed via pip --target for single-file distribution
  4. Inspect and rewrite the shebang interpreter of an existing archive by re-creating it with a new interpreter value
  5. Apply include/exclude glob filtering to build minimal archives that omit C-extension packages which cannot run from a zip
