zipfile

Data Compression and Archiving

Python documentation

Inspect a ZIP archive's central directory and report a bounded, read-only member listing with per-member metadata (name, sizes, compression method, CRC, timestamp, directory flag) without extracting any member data.

APIs

  • zipfile.ZipFile (opened in mode 'r'; provides infolist(), namelist(), getinfo(), testzip(), and close())
  • zipfile.ZipInfo (attributes filename, file_size, compress_size, compress_type, CRC, date_time, and method is_dir())
  • zipfile.is_zipfile (magic-number validity check before opening)
  • zipfile.BadZipFile (raised for malformed archives)
  • zipfile.LargeZipFile (raised when ZIP64 is required but disabled)

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"archive_path":{"type":"string","description":"Filesystem path to the ZIP archive to inspect."},"metadata_encoding":{"type":["string","null"],"description":"Optional codec name used to decode member names and comments."},"max_members":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":100000,"description":"Upper bound on members returned; listing is truncated beyond this."},"include_crc_check":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, run testzip() to validate CRCs (reads all member data)."}},"required":["archive_path"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"is_valid_zip":{"type":"boolean"},"member_count":{"type":"integer"},"truncated":{"type":"boolean"},"first_bad_member":{"type":["string","null"]},"members":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"is_dir":{"type":"boolean"},"file_size":{"type":"integer"},"compress_size":{"type":"integer"},"compress_type":{"type":"integer"},"crc":{"type":"integer"},"date_time":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"integer"},"minItems":6,"maxItems":6}},"required":["name","is_dir","file_size","compress_size","compress_type","crc","date_time"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"required":["is_valid_zip","member_count","truncated","first_bad_member","members"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only. Opens the archive for reading and closes it; no members are extracted and no files are written to disk. If include_crc_check is true, all member data is decompressed in memory for CRC verification, which consumes CPU and memory proportional to archive contents. No network access and no mutation of the source archive.

Constraints Requires a seekable file for modes 'r' and 'a'. Multipart ZIP files are not supported. Decryption of encrypted members is supported but slow (native Python). Writing encrypted archives is not supported. Optional compression modules (zlib, bz2, lzma, compression.zstd) must be present for corresponding methods. ZIP64 archives over 4 GiB are handled only when allowZip64 is enabled. Member name encoding is an instance-wide setting via metadata_encoding. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • FileNotFoundError when archive_path does not exist or is not readable.
  • BadZipFile when the file is not a valid ZIP archive or its central directory is corrupt.
  • LargeZipFile when the archive requires ZIP64 support that is not enabled.
  • KeyError from getinfo() if a member name is requested that is not present.
  • NotImplementedError when a member uses an unsupported compression method during CRC validation.
  • RuntimeError when a required optional compression module (zlib, bz2, lzma, compression.zstd) is unavailable.
  • ValueError when operating on a closed ZipFile handle.
  • OSError for I/O errors, permission problems, or resource exhaustion while reading.

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight validation of uploaded or generated ZIP archives before any extraction, using is_zipfile and testzip to detect corruption early.
  2. Building an inventory/manifest of archive contents (names, sizes, compression ratios, timestamps) for indexing, auditing, or deduplication pipelines.
  3. Guarding against decompression bombs by inspecting declared file_size and member counts before deciding whether to extract.
  4. Detecting path-traversal or absolute-path member names in untrusted archives prior to extraction.
  5. Selective retrieval planning: choosing which members to read via ZipFile.open/read based on metadata without extracting the whole archive.

Python documentation

Inspect a ZIP archive as a zipimport source: construct a zipimporter for a given archivepath (optionally with an in-archive subpath prefix) and report, for a requested dotted module name, whether it is importable, whether it is a package, its __file__ value, and whether source is present — without executing the module.

  • zipimport.zipimporter(archivepath)
  • zipimporter.find_spec(fullname, target=None)

  • zipimporter.get_filename(fullname)
  • zipimporter.get_source(fullname)
  • zipimporter.get_data(pathname)
  • zipimporter.archive
  • zipimporter.prefix
  • zipimport.ZipImportError

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"archivepath":{"type":"string","description":"Path to a ZIP file, or a path within a ZIP file (e.g. \u0027foo/bar.zip/lib\u0027)."},"fullname":{"type":"string","description":"Dotted module name to probe, e.g. \u0027pkg.mod\u0027."},"includeSource":{"type":"boolean","description":"If true, also attempt get_source and report presence/length.","default":false}},"required":["archivepath","fullname"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"archive":{"type":"string"},"prefix":{"type":"string"},"found":{"type":"boolean"},"isPackage":{"type":["boolean","null"]},"filename":{"type":["string","null"]},"hasSource":{"type":["boolean","null"]},"sourceLength":{"type":["integer","null"]}},"required":["archive","prefix","found","isPackage","filename","hasSource","sourceLength"],"additionalProperties":false}

Constraints Requires a readable local filesystem path to a ZIP archive; archivepath may include an in-archive subpath prefix. Only .py and .pyc entries are considered importable; dynamic modules are disallowed. ZIP64 supported since 3.13; Zstandard-compressed entries supported since 3.15; archives with comments supported since 3.8. find_loader/find_module were removed in 3.12, so find_spec must be used. This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ZipImportError raised by zipimporter constructor when archivepath is not a valid ZIP archive (surfaced as a structured error, not a crash).
  • ZipImportError from is_package/get_filename/get_source when the module cannot be found in the archive.
  • get_source returns None when the module exists but the archive contains no source (e.g. only .pyc).
  • OSError from get_data when the requested pathname is absent.
  • Dynamic modules (.pyd/.so) inside the archive are not importable via zipimport and will not be reported as found.
  • Malformed or truncated ZIP entries, or unsupported compression, may raise errors during inspection.

Ranked use cases

  1. Pre-flight validation that a plugin ZIP bundle exposes an expected top-level module or package before adding it to sys.path.
  2. Inventorying which modules and packages a distributed ZIP archive provides, including subpath-prefixed layouts.
  3. Detecting source-less (.pyc-only) archives to warn about slower import behavior.
  4. Diagnosing import failures by distinguishing 'module absent' from 'invalid archive' via ZipImportError.
  5. Auditing archive contents for disallowed dynamic modules (.pyd/.so) that zipimport cannot load.

zlib

Data Compression and Archiving

Python documentation

zlib_compress_bytes: compress a single in-memory bytes payload with zlib.compress, returning the compressed bytes plus the Adler-32 checksum of the original input for integrity verification.

APIs

  • zlib.compress(data, level=Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION, wbits=MAX_WBITS) — performs the one-shot deflate compression of the input bytes and returns a bytes object; this is the core operation.
  • zlib.adler32(data, value=1) — computes the unsigned 32-bit Adler-32 checksum of the original uncompressed input, used as an integrity tag in the result.
  • zlib.error — exception type raised on compression errors, mapped to a structured failure.

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"data":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded bytes to compress"},"level":{"type":"integer","minimum":-1,"maximum":9,"default":-1,"description":"Compression level; -1 default, 0 none, 1 best speed, 9 best compression"},"wbits":{"type":"integer","default":15,"description":"Window bits / header format; 9..15 zlib header, -9..-15 raw, 25..31 gzip"}},"required":["data"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"compressed":{"type":"string","description":"Base64-encoded compressed bytes"},"inputLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"outputLength":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"adler32":{"type":"integer","minimum":0,"maximum":4294967295,"description":"Unsigned 32-bit Adler-32 checksum of the original input"}},"required":["compressed","inputLength","outputLength","adler32"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Pure in-memory computation; no filesystem, network or global state changes. Returns a new bytes object and an integer checksum. No side effects beyond CPU and memory consumption.

Constraints Requires a CPython build with the optional zlib module present; zlib is optional and may be absent depending on the distributor. Behavior of wbits ranges and available constants (e.g. Z_RLE, Z_FIXED, Z_BLOCK) depends on the linked zlib version. Not cryptographically strong; checksums must not be used for authentication. Single-shot API only; streaming inputs are out of scope for this operation.

Failure modes

  • zlib.error raised by zlib.compress on compression failure (e.g. invalid internal state) — surfaced as a structured error.
  • Invalid level outside -1..9 or invalid wbits range — rejected before calling the API.
  • Input not valid base64 or not decodable to bytes — rejected with a validation error.
  • Memory exhaustion for very large inputs since the operation is one-shot and holds full input and output in memory.
  • Module unavailable in the interpreter build (zlib is an optional module) — reported as an environment error, not a compression error.

Ranked use cases

  1. Compress small-to-medium byte payloads (e.g. serialized records) before storage or transport, with an Adler-32 integrity tag for verification.
  2. Produce zlib-format or gzip-format (via wbits 25..31) compressed blobs for interoperability with gzip-compatible consumers.
  3. Generate deterministic compressed fixtures and checksums for testing compression pipelines.
  4. Pre-compress configuration or asset blobs in build tooling to reduce artifact size.
  5. Compute and attach checksums to compressed data so downstream decompression can validate integrity.

zoneinfo

Data Types

Python documentation

Resolve a single IANA time zone key to a validated ZoneInfo descriptor: construct ZoneInfo(key) (primary constructor, cached), read its key attribute, and report the UTC offset and tzname for a caller-supplied local datetime, without mutating module state.

APIs

  • zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(key) — concrete datetime.tzinfo subclass; primary constructor resolves the key against TZPATH then tzdata and raises ValueError for non-conforming keys or ZoneInfoNotFoundError when unresolved
  • zoneinfo.ZoneInfo.key — read-only attribute returning the lookup key used to construct the zone
  • zoneinfo.ZoneInfoNotFoundError — KeyError subclass raised when the key is not found on the time zone path
  • zoneinfo.available_timezones() — returns the set of valid canonical IANA keys available on the time zone path (used only for optional membership pre-check)
  • datetime.datetime(..., tzinfo=ZoneInfo(key)) — attaches the zone to a naive local datetime to derive utcoffset() and tzname()

Input contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string","description":"IANA zone key, relative normalized POSIX path form, e.g. America/Los_Angeles"},"local_datetime":{"type":"string","description":"Naive ISO 8601 local datetime, e.g. 2020-11-01T01:00:00"},"fold":{"type":"integer","enum":[0,1],"default":0}},"required":["key","local_datetime"],"additionalProperties":false}

Output contract

{"type":"object","properties":{"key":{"type":"string"},"utc_offset_seconds":{"type":"integer"},"tzname":{"type":["string","null"]},"fold":{"type":"integer"},"is_ambiguous":{"type":"boolean"}},"required":["key","utc_offset_seconds","tzname","fold","is_ambiguous"],"additionalProperties":false}

Effects Read-only with respect to time zone data: constructs or retrieves a cached ZoneInfo instance, which may populate the ZoneInfo class cache and may open files on TZPATH. Does not call reset_tzpath() or clear_cache(), so TZPATH and cache state are not modified. No network access; no writes to disk.

Constraints Not available on WASI/WebAssembly. Requires system time zone data or the tzdata package; on Windows system data is typically absent so tzdata is required. TZPATH entries must be absolute paths. ZoneInfo objects created via from_file cannot be pickled and are out of scope here. Keys are primary keys, not user-facing labels (CLDR recommended for display). This is a design proposal only; no installation, availability on any worker, or execution is claimed.

Failure modes

  • ValueError from ZoneInfo(key) when key is not a relative normalized POSIX path or contains up-level references
  • ZoneInfoNotFoundError (KeyError subclass) when no matching file exists on TZPATH and tzdata is unavailable
  • ValueError when local_datetime is not a valid naive ISO 8601 datetime
  • TypeError when fold is not an integer 0 or 1
  • InvalidTZPathWarning may be emitted at import/reset time if PYTHONTZPATH contains relative components; not raised by this operation itself

Ranked use cases

  1. Capability builders validating that a requested IANA zone key resolves before scheduling or timestamping work
  2. Normalizing event timestamps to a target zone by deriving UTC offset and tzname for a given local datetime
  3. Detecting ambiguous local times around DST transitions via fold and offset comparison
  4. Pre-flight checks that a worker environment has usable time zone data (system or tzdata) for a required key
  5. Producing canonical zone identifiers for storage and interchange instead of user-facing display strings
